Rehabilitation of Reinforced Concrete Beams Exposed to Loss of Flexural Strength by Embedded Steel Bars with Numerically Confinement Steel Plate
papers.summary: A comprehensive nonlinear finite element analysis was conducted to investigate the rehabilitation of reinforced concrete beams that have suffered a significant loss of flexural strength. The proposed rehabilitation strategy integrates near-surface-mounted (NSM) embedded steel bars with externally bonded (EB) steel plate confinement, offering a cost-effective and mechanically reliable alternative to fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP)-based methods. Numerical simulations in ABAQUS assessed the effects of key parameters, including the number, length, and equivalent area of embedded steel bars, the confinement length of steel plates, the presence or absence of lap splices, the loading type, and the concrete compressive strength. Model validation against experimental data showed close agreement in ultimate load, deflection, and load–deflection response. Results demonstrated that NSM steel bars partially restored flexural capacity, while the addition of confinement steel plates substantially improved both strength recovery and deformability. Increased confinement length and continuous main reinforcement were especially effective, resulting in load capacities surpassing those of undamaged control beams. Repeated loading negatively impacted NSM-only systems, whereas NSM–EB rehabilitation achieved significant load recovery. Higher concrete compressive strength further enhanced load recovery but reduced deformation capacity. These findings establish that the combined application of embedded steel bars and confinement steel plates is an efficient repairing strategy for damaged RC beams.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of ECAP and CECAP on Microstructure Mechanical Properties and Electrical Conductivity of Commercially Pure Copper: Experimental and Numerical Study
papers.summary: In this study, the microstructural evolution, mechanical behavior, and electrical conductivity of commercially pure copper (Cu) processed by conventional equal channel angular pressing (ECAP) and a hybrid continuous extrusion–ECAP (CECAP) processes were systematically investigated using a combination of numerical simulation and experimental characterization. Finite element simulations revealed that the CECAP process imposes substantially higher stress and plastic strain compared to ECAP, with maximum effective strain reaching approximately 3.5, which is about 75% higher than that obtained by ECAP under identical conditions (2.0). Mechanical testing demonstrated an ultrafine-grained (UFG) copper with a pronounced increase in yield strength for both ECAP- and CECAP-processed samples relative to the as-received condition, accompanied by a substantial reduction in ductility. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed a severe grain refinement, with a decrease in the average crystallite size from ~200 nm in the raw material to ~145 nm after ECAP (ultrafine-grained regime) and ~67 nm after CECAP (nanostructured regime), indicating a transition from ultrafine-grained to nanostructured copper. Electrical conductivity measurements showed a slight reduction after SPD processing, decreasing from 82.9% IACS in the raw material to 81.8% IACS after ECAP and 81.2% IACS after CECAP, indicating that the severe grain refinement and increased dislocation density have a marginal effect on electron transport properties. Overall, the results demonstrate that CECAP is a highly efficient SPD technique for imposing very high plastic strain in fewer passes, producing ultrafine/nanostructured copper with significantly enhanced strength (362 MPa yield strength, representing a 352% increase over the as-received condition) while maintaining acceptable electrical conductivity (81.2% IACS) and sufficient ductility (16.3% elongation) for many engineering applications. Despite the inherent strength-

papers.title: Calcination-Induced Structural Evolution of Nickel Phosphate and Its Impact on Charge-Storage Kinetics
papers.summary: Supercapattery performance is governed by the intrinsic properties of its electrode materials, particularly the relationship between microstructure and electrochemical behaviour. In a previous study, amorphous nickel phosphate (NP) has shown superior electrochemical performance as a battery-type electrode despite the common expectation that crystalline materials perform better in electrochemical response. In this work, NP was synthesized via a sonochemical route and its crystallinity was modulated by varying calcination temperatures. At lower calcination temperatures (300–600 ºC), NPs remain predominantly amorphous but turn crystalline when higher temperatures are applied. The thermal treatment also influenced the degree of hydration, particle morphology and pore structure. Among all temperatures, NP calcined at lower temperatures delivered the higher specific capacity and showed predominantly diffusion-influenced Faradaic kinetics. In contrast, NP calcined at higher temperatures showed lower specific capacity, but a stronger surface-control contribution to charge storage. These findings demonstrate that a high degree of crystallinity does not necessarily guarantee high charge-storage capacity and reveal a clear trade-off between active-site utilization and reaction kinetics during the amorphous to crystalline evolution of NP.

papers.title: Groundwater and surface water quality under urbanization pressure: A water quality index assessment in Siliguri Planning Area, India
papers.summary: Safe drinking water and sustainable water resource management require routine evaluations of groundwater and surface water quality. Rapidly expanding urban areas depend heavily upon these crucial assessments. Consequently, the spatial distribution of water quality parameters within the Siliguri Planning Area of West Bengal, India, was evaluated in this work. The Water Quality Index (WQI) was also calculated for both groundwater and surface water resources. The Weighted Arithmetic Water Quality Index method categorized the overall condition of these hydrological resources. A spectrum ranging from good to very poor conditions (WQI ranging from 34.02 to 182.30) defines the current groundwater quality. Elevated nitrate (up to 118 mg/L), iron (0.55 mg/L), and potassium concentrations heavily contaminate the central and southeastern urban zones. Strong positive relationships among nitrate, sodium, and sulphate (r > 0.90) were identified through correlation analysis. Human-driven pollution from agricultural runoff and domestic sewage is clearly indicated by these substantial linkages. Notable spatial variation characterized the surface water quality, with SWQI scores fluctuating between 12 and 76.97. Elevated BOD, TDS, and chloride concentrations drove a progressive deterioration along the urban corridors of the Mahananda River. Conversely, relatively healthy conditions were maintained throughout the Balason River. Agricultural activities, improper waste disposal, and intense urbanization severely impact these vital reserves. Immediate intervention is absolutely necessary to halt this widespread degradation. Ultimately, policymakers and civic authorities can construct targeted water quality management strategies using these empirical results. The design of vital treatment infrastructure throughout the region can be supported by the scientific foundation presented in this study.

papers.title: Soil Erosion Versus Soil Retention Capacity: An Impact Assessment Of Regulating Ecosystem Service Provision In Iran
papers.summary: The objective of this study was to determine the impact of erosion on soil retention as an ecosystem service and its relationship with soil quality in a mountainous catchment in Iran. In this regard, 42 soil samples were collected from rangelands, rainfed, and irrigated farming areas. Thirteen physical and chemical soil attributes were measured. Principal component analysis was applied to identify a soil quality index (SQI). The respective ranges of soil erosion rates from rangelands, rainfed farming lands, and irrigated farming lands were estimated to be 0.2 – 46.4, 0.18 – 0.20, and 0.00 – 0.18 t ha −1 yr −1. The SQI estimates ranged between 3.2 – 4.0 for the rangelands compared with corresponding estimates of 4.0 – 5.7 for the rainfed farming lands and 5.7 – 8.4 for the irrigated farming lands. Soil retention was estimated to range between 0 – 0.01 t ha −1 yr −1 (average = 0.005 t ha −1 yr −1) for rangelands, 0.01 – 0.03 t ha −1 yr −1 (average = 0.02 t ha −1 yr −1) for rainfed farmlands, and 0.03 – 3.5 t ha −1 yr −1 (average = 1.8 t ha −1 yr −1) for irrigated farming lands. Negative relationships were observed among soil erosion, soil quality, and soil retention, emphasising the sensitivity of soil quality to the soil erosion rates estimated for different land use types. This study provides evidence for the negative effects of soil erosion under different land uses regarding the degradation of soil quality and soil retention as an ecosystem service.

papers.title: Infiltration in Three Planting Media at Two Chili Growth Phases
papers.summary: Infiltration under rainfall is relevant to water management in container cultivation. This study described the infiltration rate of three planting media (clay, loamy sand, and sandy clay loam) planted with bird’s eye chili (Capsicum frutescens L.) at the vegetative and generative phases. Planter bags were tested with a rainfall simulator on nine days per phase. Infiltration rate was obtained from the water balance between applied rainfall (16.98 mm/h) and surface runoff at 2-minute intervals and fitted to the Kostiakov equation. Infiltration rate declined with time in all 54 recorded series. Mean initial rate was highest in loamy sand (15.68 mm/h), followed by sandy clay loam (14.47 mm/h) and clay (13.86 mm/h); final rates followed the same order (9.90, 9.33, and 8.74 mm/h). Initial rate was 0.85 mm/h higher in the generative than in the vegetative phase, whereas the phase comparison of final rates was inconclusive. Time to constant rate was longest in loamy sand and longer in the generative phase, while the rate of decline did not differ detectably. Initial rate was negatively associated with antecedent sensor moisture. The rates changed in discrete steps and declined nearly linearly before leveling off. Kostiakov exponents ranged from −0.311 to −0.144 (R² = 0.81–0.98). Because no unplanted control was included, the results do not isolate an effect of chili plants or their roots.

papers.title: Water and soil loss from purple soil surface under simulated rainfall in Sichuan Basin, Southwest China
papers.source: Journal of Soil Science and Environmental Management
papers.summary: The relationship between rainfall, runoff and soil loss from different slope angles of purple soil still remain unclear despite numerous studies. This study was carried out in the laboratory to estimate runoff and sediment yield from different slope angles (5°, 10°, 15°, 20° and 25°) using Norton rainfall simulator and soil boxes. The soil was subjected to different rainfall intensities of 0.6, 1.1, 1.5 and 1.8 mm/min. Results showed runoff rates decreased in 10° > 20° > 15° > 25° > 5° order with values ranging from 0.26 mm/min for low rainfall intensity (0.6 mm/min) on slope 5° to 1.06 mm/min for simulation experiments with higher rainfall intensity (1.8 mm/min) on slope 10°. Pearson correlation showed a strong correlation (p<0.001) between rainfall intensity and runoff rate. Soil loss linearly increased with runoff rate and slope angles (from 1255.66 gm-2 h-1 under rainfall of 1.8 mm/min on slope 25° to 55.97 gm-2h-1 under 0.6 mm/min on slope 5°). From R² values, runoff strongly explained 53 to 81% variance in the sediment detachment. Assessment of rainfall function on purple soil may help to build conservative measures and strategies in controlling soil loss under different rainfall intensities in Sichuan Basin.

papers.title: GIS-Based Groundwater Recharge and Urbanization Analysis
papers.source: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
papers.summary: Groundwater is a vital source of water for domestic, agricultural and industrial use, but rapid urbanization, population growth and over-extraction are placing it under increasing stress. The expansion of built-up areas replaces permeable ground with impervious surfaces, which reduces infiltration and natural recharge while the demand for water continues to rise. This paper presents the framework and preliminary study for a GIS-based assessment of groundwater recharge and the influence of urbanization in selected areas of Manjeri Municipality, Malappuram district, Kerala. Recent studies on GIS–AHP groundwater potential zonation, the effects of urbanization and climate variability on groundwater, the validation of groundwater potential maps and site selection for managed aquifer recharge are reviewed, and an integrated methodology is proposed that combines approximately twenty years of groundwater-level and rainfall data, Google Earth and satellite-based urbanization analysis, GIS thematic layers and statistical modelling in SPSS. The literature review and methodology are complete. Data collection, spatial analysis, modelling and field verification are planned for the next phase, so no conclusions on groundwater conditions are drawn in this paper

papers.title: An ensemble groundwater prediction (EGP) system to forecast groundwater levels in alluvial aquifers in Switzerland
papers.source: Natural hazards and earth system sciences
papers.summary: Groundwater is a key source of freshwater for drinking water supply and agricultural irrigation on a global scale. Groundwater in Switzerland (and beyond) is traditionally regarded as a reliable source of freshwater. Recent extreme drought events (i.e. in 2018, 2022, and 2026) have shown, however, that groundwater responds to these events and can cause problems for water supply and groundwater availability. With hydrological extremes becoming more frequent, there is a growing need for early warning systems and improved forecasting. This study develops and tests a scalable ensemble groundwater prediction (EGP) system with a 32 d lead time. The system combines extended-range precipitation and temperature forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) with the lumped-parameter groundwater model Pastas. Forecasts were evaluated at six monitoring wells across Switzerland, representing diverse hydrogeological settings, and compared to naive persistence and climatology benchmarks. Results indicate that the EGP system produces skillful forecasts up to 32 d ahead, with Spearman correlations between 0.73–0.99 for one to four weeks ahead. The required model–data complexity to provide skillful forecasts varies. In aquifers with long response times and memory, forecasts driven by recent measurements of precipitation and temperature, as well as climatology, are sufficient. In fast-responding, short-memory systems, however, using meteorological forecasts of precipitation and temperature adds clear value and improves groundwater level forecasts compared with using only recent meteorological measurements and system memory. Forecast skill in mountainous regions (e.g. Davos) remains limited because local meteorology is difficult to predict. These findings highlight both the potential and the limitations of short-term groundwater forecasting.

papers.title: GIS-based inverse hydrogeological budget application to evaluate groundwater recharge of the karst aquifer feeding the Sanità Spring (Caposele, South Italy)
papers.summary: Estimating groundwater recharge in karst aquifers is a crucial need for sustainable water management under escalating climate pressures in the Mediterranean region and increasing groundwater demand. For this reason, quantifying recharge in these complex hydrogeological settings, where water infiltration is heavily influenced by seasonality, remains challenging due to localized infiltration pathways and missing parameters in conventional surface water balances. To overcome these limitations, spatially discretized inverse water budget approaches offer an alternative by integrating long-term hydro-meteorological datasets with distributed land cover and geological properties. The main objective of this study is to estimate groundwater recharge of the karst hydrogeological basin feeding the Sanità spring at Caposele (NE Campania Region, Southern Italy), the main spring of the Sele River, serving as the key source of the historic Apulian Aqueduct, which provides drinking water to over four million inhabitants, across Puglia (100% of the population), Basilicata (25% of the population) and Campania (2% of the population). For this reason, in this study the groundwater recharge assessment for the Sanità spring has been carried out by applying a GIS-based Inverse Hydrogeological Budget methodology proposed by Civita, using climate parameters for the period (2000–2025), providing a reproducible framework to support water management in this vulnerable karst catchment area.

papers.title: Flooded Rivers, Drying Wetlands, Vanishing Tributaries: An Apparent Hydrological Paradox in the East Ganga Plains
papers.summary: The East Ganga Plains present an apparent hydrological paradox: embanked rivers continue to flood, yet adjacent wetlands and small streams are drying and groundwater levels are falling. We test whether these changes are mutually consistent in the Kosi–Gandak interfan, the most wetland-rich part of the Ganga Plains outside the delta. We use 35 years of Landsat imagery, terrain height above the nearest channel, rainfall and flood records, monitoring wells and GRACE gravity data. Although rainfall shows no trend (1990–2024), surface wetness declined significantly across 58% of the interfan and vegetation greenness rose by 46% over 1988–2022. Small streams dried after the monsoon, and the pre-monsoon and monsoon water table deepened by ~5 cm yr⁻¹ across north Bihar (2000–2022). Because 72% of wetland pixels lie no more than 0.25 m above the nearest channel, natural relief alone cannot explain the drying; embankment disconnection is the most likely explanation, though confirming causation requires direct observations of river–floodplain exchange. Well-based groundwater storage tracks wetland inundation interannually (r = 0.58, p = 0.005, n = 22), independently of trends and monsoon rainfall. Storage recovered in 2007–2008 and 2020–2021, when embankment breaches and overbank flooding reconnected rivers with floodplains, inundating up to 24% of the floodplain (median 4% in non-flood years). Detrended greenness varies inversely with inundation, whereas greenness and groundwater have opposing trends but uncorrelated interannual variations, consistent with intensifying irrigation pumping. GRACE records a larger regional decline but does not resolve this local relationship, indicating that gravity data and wells capture different processes. Groundwater decline in this wetland-rich plain, where floodplain recharge should be most effective, indicates severe stress. papers.title: Disentangling the Response of Vegetation to Precipitation in a Changing Climate: A Frequency-Domain Analysis Using Long-Term Earth Observations
Efforts Toward Zero Run-off through Rainwater Infiltration Well Planning (Case Study: Dramaga Cantik Residence Block A-E)
papers.summary: Dramaga Cantik Residence Blocks A–E in Bogor Regency experience increased stormwater runoff due to land-use changes that reduce natural infiltration areas. This study aims to estimate runoff volume and determine the required dimensions and number of infiltration wells as a runoff management strategy based on the zero-run-off concept. The analysis used 20 years of maximum daily rainfall data, the Rational Method, and soil infiltration measurements using a double-ring infiltrometer. The Log-Pearson Type III distribution yielded a design rainfall of 128 mm/day for a 2-year return period, while the average infiltration rate was 6.6 cm/h. The proposed design comprises 154 cylindrical concrete infiltration wells, each with a diameter of 1.5 m and a depth of 2.5 m. Design calculations estimate that the system could manage rooftop runoff and reduce the total site runoff volume from 1,478.04 m³ to 828.20 m³, representing a calculated reduction of 43.97%. The estimated construction cost is IDR 1.73 billion. These findings indicate the potential of infiltration well planning to manage stormwater runoff and enhance on-site infiltration. However, the estimated performance and technical applicability require further field verification. Routine maintenance and complementary runoff management measures for roads and other impervious surfaces are also necessary to support progress toward zero run-off conditions.

papers.title: Event-driven changes in surface-soil hydraulic properties in semi-arid regions may drive shifts in surface runoff regimes over decadal timescales
papers.summary: Seasonality of rainfall and drought drives degradation and subsequent recovery of soil hydrological properties, which in turn influence water storage and runoff generation. To explore how these dynamics shape the soil water balance, we conceptualized soil hydraulic properties as a variable subject to degradation, recovery, or no change. Degradation and recovery were formulated as state-dependent processes that modify infiltration capacity, allowing rainfall under degraded conditions to generate runoff, described as infiltration and soil moisture excess. Using atmospheric forcing from southwest Australia, we simulated runoff time series differing in regimes, defined as time intervals of runoff accumulation. Applying dynamic time warping (DTW) and hierarchical clustering, the runoff time series were classified into three characteristic emergent regimes: zero or short-spanned regimes with sub-decadal decline linked to rapid recovery, persistent runoff linked to no recovery, and an intermediate pattern with moderate runoff regimes. Linear discriminant analysis (LDA) of the dimensionless model parameters revealed that rainfall frequency is the dominant driver of different clusters. Cases involving isolated rainfall are more likely to undergo persistent degradation and runoff-dominated regimes, whereas continuous rainfall events facilitate recovery of soil hydrological properties over decadal timescales. Monte Carlo analysis showed that the first and third clusters were robust to stochastic atmospheric forcing, whereas the second cluster was sensitive to stochastic variability and could be clustered differently across realizations. Decadal-scale hydrological responses to stochastic atmospheric forcing can thus emerge from the interactions between degradation and recovery with subdaily controls.

papers.title: Fluorine occurrence, leaching behavior, and environmental enrichment in coal-bearing strata of Eastern Yunnan, China
Task-Aware multi-task learning for streamflow and soil moisture prediction: a first step toward unified hydrological models
papers.summary: Streamflow and soil moisture are two critical variables in the hydrological cycle, linked through infiltration, runoff generation, and groundwater recharge. Traditional forecasting approaches often treat them independently, overlooking interdependencies and limiting predictive skill. This study investigates Multi-Task Learning (MTL) for daily prediction of both variables using the CAMELS dataset derived from the CARAVAN archive. Two task-aware architectures – a Transformer-based and a Mamba-based model – were developed, where shared representations are combined with task identifiers to distinguish outputs for streamflow and soil moisture. Both models were trained to produce 7-day forecasts with balanced sampling across tasks. Results across more than 600 U.S. basins show that MTL models achieve accuracy comparable to or slightly better than single-task baselines, demonstrating the feasibility of learning shared representations. By confirming that one model can distinguish between processes and predict multiple targets without loss of skill, this study establishes a proof of concept for unified, multi-variable forecasting systems.

papers.title: A modified Hardin-Drnevich model for saturated saline soils considering the effects of salt content and confining pressure
papers.summary: Saline soils are widespread in northwestern China and other parts of the world. Their salt content (SC) varies with rainfall infiltration, evaporation crystallization, groundwater level variations, and seasonal freeze-thaw cycles, which may result in strength loss and slope instability. This study examines the effects of SC and effective confining pressure (ECP) on the mechanical behavior of saturated saline soil by means of consolidated-drained (CD) triaxial tests and resonant column (RC) tests. Specimens with SCs of 0.5%, 3%, 7%, and 12% were tested under ECPs of 50, 100, and 200 kPa. The results show that the deviatoric stress–strain curves under static loading exhibited strain-softening behavior. Peak strength, peak principal stress ratio, and cohesion first increase and then decrease as SC increases, reaching their maximum values at 7% SC. In contrast, the friction angle remains largely the same. Thus, SC mainly affects strength through changes in particle bonding, cementation, and soil structure rather than interparticle friction. The maximum dynamic shear modulus rose with both SC and ECP, and a prediction model incorporating their effects showed good agreement with test data. The normalized dynamic shear modulus versus normalized shear strain curves exhibit a consistent form and can be described by a simplified Hardin-Drnevich (H-D) model. A prediction model for the reference shear strain in the modified H-D model was developed to account for the effects of SC and ECP. The dynamic shear modulus values predicted by the modified model are within ±20% of the measured values. Furthermore, a prediction model was developed for the damping ratio variation with shear strain, accounting for the effects of SC and ECP. 90% of the data fell within a relative error of ±20% between the measured and predicted values. The experimental results and proposed models provide a technical reference for geotechnical design and slope stability assessment under both static and seismi

papers.title: Hydro-Mechanical Coupling and Failure Mechanisms of a Reservoir Bank Slope Under Rainfall and Reservoir Water-Level Fluctuations: Physical Model Evidence
papers.summary: Residual gravelly soil slopes in karst reservoir areas of Southwest China are highly susceptible to hydrological coupling disasters, while their synergistic failure mechanisms under rainfall and reservoir water fluctuation remain insufficiently quantified. A 1:200 geometric-scale, 1 g physical model of the Xizhai unstable slope was tested under progressively increasing rainfall, a constant 120 mm/h rainfall-only control, independent reservoir-level fluctuation, and their combination. The results reveal three distinct failure modes: rear-edge retrogressive failure dominated by cumulative vertical rainfall infiltration (critical rainfall: 324.98 mm for progressive rainfall), toe-dominated front-edge retrogressive failure under water level fluctuation, and accelerated two-way composite failure under coupled loading. The same-series constant-intensity control was introduced to avoid conflating rainfall history with reservoir effects. Relative to progressive rainfall, constant 120 mm/h rainfall reduced first cracking from 159 to 14 min and initial sliding from 300 to 40 min. Relative to the constant 120 mm/h control, adding the reservoir cycle advanced first cracking from 14 to 7 min and initial sliding from 40 to 30 min. The combined condition produced the largest DIC active area and equivalent disturbed volume, and rapid drawdown created the critical hazard window through suction loss, seepage erosion and toe flow sliding. The mechanism-based failure modes support engineering interpretation for analogous karst reservoir slopes.

papers.title: High-resolution karst spring discharge datasets of the Euro-Mediterranean mountain regions
papers.summary: Karst groundwater systems exhibit heterogeneity in recharge, circulation, and discharge, occupying a unique position within groundwater systems. This complexity facilitates rapid responses via the preferential flow routes, making karst systems vulnerable to climatic and anthropogenic pressures. High-altitude karst aquifers are particularly susceptible to shifting climate patterns – specifically rising temperatures, declining snow cover, and increasingly less and inconsistent precipitation – within the Mediterranean climate hotspot. Effective sustainable management of these groundwater systems require robust hydrological modelling; however, the application of such models is often constrained by the availability of high-quality, reliable datasets. This study presents a comprehensive collection of high-resolution karst spring discharge data from major Euro-Mediterranean mountain belts, including the Atlas, Betics, Pyrenees, Jura, Alps, Carpathians, Apennines, Dinarides, Hellenides, Balkans, Taurus, Levant, and Zagros. We compiled a total of 129 discharge time series specifically curated for hydrological modelling. Geographically, the dataset is led by the Alps (approx. 38.7 %), followed by the Carpathians (11.7 %) and Dinarides (approx. 8.5 %), the Apennines, and Zagros each contributing approx. 6.2 %. The Levant, Pyrenees and Taurus account for approx. 5 % each, while the remaining regions (Atlas, Balkans, Betics, Hellenides, and Jura) represent less than 5 % each. In terms of temporal resolution, 92 % of the records are daily, while hourly and monthly data each comprise 4 %. The average record length is 21 years, which is led by a 98-year series from Unica Spring, Slovenia (1926–2024). Regional analysis indicates that the Jura, Balkans and Pyrenees maintain average record length exceeding 30 years of daily data, followed by the Alps, Apennines, Betics, Carpathians, and Dinarides, exceeding 20 years, whereas the Atlas, Levant, Taurus, and Zagros range between 10 and 2

papers.title: Estimation of Groundwater Recharge to the Aquifer Surrounding Buzwagi Gold Mine by Water Balance Method, in Northern Tanzania
papers.source: International journal of research and scientific innovation
papers.summary: Groundwater is an important source of water for domestic use, agriculture and mining activities in northwestern Tanzania. In the area surrounding Buzwagi Gold Mine (BGM), increasing water demand and mining-related activities highlight the need for reliable information on groundwater replenishment to support sustainable water-resource management and planning. Estimating groundwater recharge is essential because recharge represents the amount of water that replenishes the aquifer and helps assess the long-term availability of groundwater. This study aimed to estimate groundwater recharge in the aquifer surrounding Buzwagi Gold Mine using the water-balance method. A water-budget model incorporating precipitation, surface runoff, actual evapotranspiration, and changes in soil-water storage was employed. Rainfall data covering 16 years (2005–2020) were obtained from the Tanzania Meteorological Authority (TMA), while Landsat 8 satellite images for 2018 and 2020 were acquired from the USGS Global Visualization Viewer (GloVis). The satellite images were processed using supervised classification in ArcMap to identify land-use and land-cover categories and determine the composite curve number, a key parameter for estimating surface runoff. The classified land-cover categories included vegetation, built-up areas, water bodies, and barren land, resulting in a composite curve number of 76. Potential evapotranspiration was estimated using the Thornthwaite method and used to calculate actual evapotranspiration. The results indicated that actual evapotranspiration ranged from 662 to 1,435 mm year⁻¹, while surface runoff ranged from 253 to 863 mm year⁻¹. Estimated annual groundwater recharge ranged from 240 to 400 mm year⁻¹, with a mean of approximately 319 mm year⁻¹. These findings provide preliminary, site-specific estimates of groundwater recharge that can inform groundwater-resource assessment, sustainable abstraction planning, and water management in the BGM area. A key limitat

papers.title: Fuzzy logic-based geospatial distribution mapping for groundwater potential assessment
papers.summary: The Kaddam Watershed in Telangana, India, faces critical groundwater depletion due to increasing demand and limited natural recharge. In this study, we delineate groundwater potential zones (GWPZ) by integrating fuzzy logic with geospatial datasets in ArcGIS. Seven fuzzy membership functions, including MS Small, MS Large, Gaussian, Large, Near, Small, and Linear, were applied to key thematic layers, including land use/land cover, drainage density, slope, rainfall, and lineament density. The resulting groundwater potential map was classified into four categories: Excellent, Good, Moderate, and Moderate to Poor. Comparative analysis revealed that the MS Small function produces the most balanced and hydrologically meaningful spatial distribution, with membership value ranges of 0.12–0.33 for Excellent and 0.51–1.00 for Moderate to Poor. Other functions, such as Gaussian and Near, emphasize mid range suitability, while Linear shows broad transitions across categories. Validation using observed groundwater levels from six wells shows strong agreement, with an accuracy of approximately 83% for the MS Small function. Spatially, Excellent and Good zones are primarily located in gently sloping areas with high lineament density and favorable drainage conditions supporting infiltration and recharge. The prime contribution of this research is the empirical comparison of seven fuzzy membership functions within a single watershed, combined with a histogram-based thresholding method and field validation. This study provides a robust and scalable framework for groundwater prospect mapping and sustainable water resource planning. Our approach minimizes subjectivity and offers practical guidance for planners and water resource managers.

papers.title: Seasonal Groundwater Changes in the Ganga and Godavari Basins from GRACE: Implications for Managed Aquifer Recharge and Climate Adaptation
papers.summary: India extracts more groundwater than any other country, yet seasonal depletion remains poorly quantified because most basin-scale studies rely on annual averages that mask dry-season deficits. We quantify and compare seasonal groundwater storage in two contrasting Indian basins, the alluvial Ganga (838,803 km²) and the hard-rock Godavari (312,150 km²), from 2002 to 2025, using a reproducible Python workflow combining GRACE and GRACE Follow-On CSR RL06 mascon data with GLDAS Noah v2.1 soil moisture, snow water equivalent and canopy water. Groundwater is isolated by subtracting these storage terms from the GRACE signal; evapotranspiration and runoff are fluxes, not stores, and are not subtracted. Three checkpoint years (2015, 2020, 2025) are disaggregated into pre-monsoon, monsoon and post-monsoon panels. Ganga pre-monsoon storage ratchets from −13.2 cm in 2015 to − 21.3 cm in 2025, never recovering to positive values, whereas Godavari pre-monsoon storage fluctuates non-monotonically between −1.5 and +3.0 cm and returns to a positive post-monsoon anomaly each year. This implies a water-equivalent deficit of approximately 179 km³ for the Ganga and a small surplus of about 3.7 km³ for the Godavari at the 2025 pre-monsoon. These findings translate directly into climate adaptation guidance: Managed Aquifer Recharge should be sized against the pre-monsoon deficit rather than the annual mean, with percolation structures suited to the Deccan hard rock and injection wells or flood-spreading in the alluvial Ganga. This gives water managers a measurable, satellite-derived basis for adapting recharge infrastructure to intensifying seasonal stress under a changing monsoon.

papers.title: When does fractional creep indicate landslide acceleration? Evidence from multi-site landslide monitoring records
papers.summary: Fractional viscoelastic creep models are increasingly fitted to landslide displacement records for acceleration monitoring and warning, yet what the fitted fractional order can and cannot deliver operationally remains poorly tested. We evaluate fractional Burgers creep indicators across contrasting regimes – near-linear steady creep, groundwater-pulse acceleration, monotonic failure acceleration, and two reservoir-driven slopes – together with failure-time estimation, rolling-origin forecast validation, driving models, and a physics-informed neural network consistency check (details in a companion methods paper). On near-linear steady creep the fractional model is rejected as over-parameterisation; on the monotonic Achoma record the order is cleanly identified (α = 4.456) and Fukuzono extrapolation matches the observed failure time to within a day, but a rolling-origin check shows this agreement is retrospective: a convergent forecast is available only 3–4 days before failure. On the pulse record (Gradenbach), a fading-memory Abel kernel (β = 0.139) decouples groundwater-driven pulses from the long-term trend and removes the trade-off ridge of plain Burgers. The reservoir cases expose omitted-driver dangers: with explicit seasonal reservoir stress, Baijiabao's order falls from 1.228 to 0.715 and 48% of the annual-cycle residual is absorbed, while Shuping's α = 3.616 most plausibly reflects the reservoir-driven seasonal step rather than a pre-failure signal. We conclude that α > 1 marks entry into accelerating creep without predicting failure time, and that unmodelled periodic forcing is absorbed as spurious super-linear order; identifiability checks and an explicit driving model must accompany any warning use of the fitted order.

papers.title: Geotechnical Engineering of Lateral Soil Movement and Subsidence in Bojong Koneng, Bogor Regency
papers.summary: Bojong Koneng Village, Babakan Madang District, Bogor Regency, is highly susceptible to lateral ground movement and potential land subsidence due to weathered clay shale, hilly topography, high rainfall, and expanding built-up areas. This study aimed to identify the factors controlling ground instability, establish a conceptual model of ground movement mechanisms, and propose an integrated geotechnical mitigation strategy. A descriptive-analytical approach was employed using secondary geological, soil, topographic, hydrological, land-use, ground movement hazard, and surface deformation data, supplemented by visual field observations. Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) data indicated a low-resistivity zone at approximately 8–15 m depth, potentially associated with clay-rich, weathered, and water-saturated materials within the Jatiluhur Formation. Ground movement susceptibility was classified into four categories, with high-hazard zones predominantly concentrated in the eastern and southern areas. Surface deformation was categorized as low, moderate, high, and very high, with the highest deformation rates exceeding 60 mm/year in the eastern and southeastern areas. The proposed conceptual mechanism involved rainfall infiltration, increased pore water pressure, reduced effective stress, and progressive deterioration of weathered clay shale shear strength, potentially leading to slope creep and translational landslides. Recommended mitigation options included improved surface and subsurface drainage, soil nailing, shotcrete reinforcement, polymer–calcite precipitation (PCP), gabion retaining structures, and an early warning system (EWS). These measures require site-specific geotechnical investigations and engineering validation before implementation.

papers.title: New insights from fully-integrated surface-subsurface hydrological modeling in high-elevation glaciated environments
papers.summary: Recent modeling efforts go towards distributed physics-based modeling for improved hydrological process understanding. The sparse hydro-meteorological observations and complex topography in high-elevation mountainous environments have, however, hampered the application of such data-intensive and sophisticated techniques for detailed process exploration. In particular, characterizing surface-subsurface water exchange processes in these terrains remains understudied. Here we implement a fully-integrated and fully-distributed surface-subsurface hydrological model, WaSiM, to quantify the observed daily streamflow variations and their interactions with groundwater in the high-elevation glaciated catchment (Martell Valley) in the central European Alps since the 2000s. Extensive field observations (meteorology, vegetation, glacier mass balance, soil properties, river discharge), especially in-situ groundwater levels, were collected to investigate hydrological processes and constrain model parameters in the surface and subsurface. We observe that in contrast to the delayed responses typically observed in aquifers, shallow alpine groundwater responds nearly as quickly as streamflow to peak snowmelt and extreme rainfall events, highlighting the need for improved subsurface parametrization in hydrological modeling. Joint evaluation against shallow groundwater heads and streamflow shows that the daily streamflow and shallow groundwater dynamics can be reproduced without requiring the WaSiM interflow component, providing new constraints on the representation of unsaturated-zone flow pathways in high Alpine hydrological models. Moreover, to improve the integration of point-scale groundwater observations into fully-distributed models, we suggest pre-calculating the Topographic Wetness Index to stratify hydro-topographic settings and combining this information with other site characteristics to guide piezometer placement. Despite uncertainties associated with model structure and su

papers.title: The convective switch: unveiling alpine landslide triggers via high-resolution topography and geomorphologically constrained deep learning
papers.summary: Data-driven models have increasingly dominated landslide susceptibility mapping, yet regional studies often rely on coarse-resolution data and uninterpretable architectures. This study proposes a geomorphologically constrained, dual-branch deep learning framework to predict rainfall-induced landslides in the Tyrolean Alps, bridging the gap between empirical algorithms and topographic determinism. To capture regional moisture dynamics, 30-day continuous antecedent precipitation sequences from reanalysis data were fused with highly localized 5-m resolution morphometric derivatives. The model was evaluated using strict spatial cross-validation to account for spatial autocorrelation, and an integrated gradients framework was applied to achieve interpretability. The model achieved a robust, spatially validated performance, quantitatively revealing a delayed hydrological response where antecedent rainfall serves as a critical prerequisite for landslide initiation. Furthermore, a geomorphological constraint (slopes ≤15° = 0 probability) successfully eliminated false-positive artifacts in valley bottoms. These results demonstrate that integrating regional dynamic meteorological memory with high-resolution topographic constraints is essential for identifying micro-scale structural traps, paving the way for advanced predictive hazard assessments.

papers.title: Assessing Permeable Pavements and Urban Layouts Designed to Absorb Stormwater and Mitigate Flood Risks
papers.source: International Journal of Science Strategic Management and Technology
papers.summary: Urban flooding increasingly reflects the interaction of high imperviousness, short-duration intense rainfall, constrained drainage networks, and spatially concentrated runoff. Permeable pavements can transform roads, parking areas, sidewalks, and courtyards from runoff-generating surfaces into distributed storage and infiltration systems, but their effectiveness depends as much on urban layout, loading ratio, soil conditions, drainage configuration, maintenance, and storm magnitude as on pavement material. This paper develops a data-driven assessment of permeable pavements and spatial low-impact-development (LID) layouts using published field observations and recent city-scale modeling evidence. The evidence base includes monitored permeable-pavement installations in North Carolina, New Hampshire, Wisconsin, and northern Ohio, together with a 2026 optimized retrofit study of an older urban community that used EPA SWMM, observed 2024 rainfall events, and explicit placement of permeable pavements, rain gardens, and green roofs. Field studies show that properly designed permeable pavements can sharply reduce surface runoff and delay peaks; a monitored porous-asphalt system in New Hampshire reduced peak flow by approximately 90%, while broader Great Lakes evidence reports event-volume reductions ranging from about 13% to nearly 99% depending on site and design. In the 2026 urban-layout case, optimized LID deployment reduced stormwater runoff by roughly 59% and total suspended solids loads by about 79%; peak TSS concentrations during the 20-year design storm decreased from 132.22 to 45.72 mg/L, while observed 2024 storm events also showed substantial reductions. The study synthesizes these data into a spatial design framework emphasizing distributed source control, targeted treatment of low-lying convergence zones, preservation of exceedance pathways, maintenance access, and matching pavement area to contributing impervious area. Results indicate that flood mitigation is

papers.title: A multi-GPU parallel framework for large-scale saturated–unsaturated flow analysis using the numerical manifold method
Fire-induced soil water repellency, CO2 efflux and organic carbon storage in sub-Saharan African savanna soils: implications for climate-smart land management
papers.summary: How does fire-induced soil water repellency (SWR) mediate post-fire soil CO 2 efflux and soil organic carbon (SOC) storage in tropical African savannas, and what fire-smart management can conserve SOC? Seasonal bush burning is deeply embedded across sub-Saharan derived savannas, yet the integrated effects of fire on soil physical, biogeochemical and carbon-cycling processes remain poorly quantified: only 17.0% of global fire-soil research originates from sub-Saharan Africa, and no studies have quantified the SWR–CO 2 –SOC interaction chain in the Nigerian derived savanna. Tropical savannas are prioritised because they store more terrestrial carbon than the atmosphere and vegetation combined, support over one billion people dependent on rain-fed agriculture, and experience fire as an annual management tool rather than an episodic disturbance. Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) is emphasised because SOC underpins CSA’s productivity, resilience and mitigation pillars, yet fire-induced SWR introduces uncertainty into the persistence of CSA-induced SOC gains. This review synthesises evidence from 135 unique peer-reviewed studies on three mechanistically coupled soil responses to fire — SWR, CO 2 efflux and SOC storage — established in temperate and Mediterranean literature but under-quantified in tropical Africa. Systematic searches across six bibliographic sources using five Boolean search blocks identified 1,150 records, of which 820 remained after duplicate removal. Inclusion required peer-reviewed quantitative evidence on fire-induced SWR, post-fire CO 2 efflux or SOC effects in tropical, subtropical or semi-arid savanna contexts. Of 360 full-text records assessed, 180 met these criteria; cross-domain deduplication removed 40 duplicate entries across thematic domains, and five methodological references were retained in the inventory but excluded from the evidence corpus, yielding 135 unique studies in the final corpus. Synthesised evidence demonstrates that fire-induced

papers.title: An optimal bulk density of 1.06 g·cm-³ sustains rhizosphere microbial–metabolite interactions and tobacco growth in clay soils
papers.summary: Introduction Soil bulk density is a core indicator of soil compaction and critically regulates rhizosphere microbial activity and plant–microbe interactions. However, the internal mechanisms through which bulk density shapes microbial functional strategies and metabolic responses remain poorly understood, especially in clay soils. Methods To elucidate how soil physical structure governs water movement, microbial community functions, and metabolite dynamics under different compaction levels, four bulk density gradients (0.74, 1.06, 1.28, 1.47 g·cm - ³) were established in clay soil via a field trial integrated with repacked soil column infiltration simulation. Multi-omics approaches including metagenomic sequencing and untargeted LC-MS metabolomics were applied to characterize rhizosphere profiles of flue-cured tobacco. Results Increasing bulk density significantly reduced wetting-front migration rates (P < 0.05), indicating impaired pore connectivity and restricted water transport. Moderate density (1.06 g·cm - ³) yielded the highest microbial α-diversity (P < 0.05) and sustained balanced plant growth. At this density, KEGG pathways related to membrane transport and signal transduction were markedly upregulated, suggesting enhanced environmental sensing and nutrient-acquisition capacity. In contrast, severe compaction (1.47 g·cm - ³) restructured co-occurrence networks into competition-dominated, densely connected but poorly modularized topologies and suppressed overall metabolic activity. Microbe–metabolite correlation analysis showed that the moderate-density treatment had the most complex interaction network (22 significant pairs), versus only 8 and 7 pairs in the two higher-density treatments, respectively. Conclusions A moderate bulk density of 1.06 g·cm - ³ optimizes soil water conditions, boosts rhizosphere microbial functional potential and metabolic interactions, and promotes tobacco growth. Therefore, this density is recommended as a practical management t

papers.title: A multi-variable lysimeter dataset for soil–atmosphere interaction studies
papers.summary: Soil–atmosphere interactions exert a fundamental control on the hydro-mechanical behaviour of shallow soils and are increasingly recognised as relevant in both hydrology and geotechnical engineering. Although these processes in silty sand and clays have been investigated by a substantial part of the literature, long-term observational datasets for silty pyroclastic soils remain scarce, despite their widespread occurrence worldwide and their frequent partially saturated state, which makes them susceptible to rainfall-induced landslides. A continuous dataset collected over four hydrological years from a physical lysimeter experiment on silty pyroclastic soils from the Campania region (Italy) is analysed. The dataset captures the coupled evolution of meteorological and hydrological forcing under well-defined boundary conditions, providing rare long-term evidence of soil–atmosphere exchange processes in this soil class. The resulting data enable robust direct and indirect estimation of key soil hydraulic properties and detailed characterization of evapotranspiration dynamics under bare soil conditions across multiple hydrological cycles. Owing to its duration, internal consistency, and multi-variable structure, the dataset represents a valuable benchmark for the calibration and validation of advanced hydro-mechanical and coupled numerical models.

papers.title: In situ xylem water isotope monitoring: from promise to practice
papers.summary: Water stable isotopes (δ²H, δ 18 O) are powerful tracers of water cycling in the groundwater–soil–plant–atmosphere continuum, yet most conventional approaches rely on destructive, labor-intensive sampling that provides only discrete temporal snapshots. In situ vapor-equilibration techniques coupled to laser spectroscopy now enable continuous monitoring of soil and xylem water isotopes, bypassing extraction artefacts and targeting the mobile water pool in both soils and plants. Building on more than a decade of methodological development, we contrast commercially available systems such as the water isotope probe (WIP) with the stem borehole equilibration (SBE) approach, highlighting their shared physical basis but differing costs, flexibility, and field practicality. We synthesize evidence that in situ datasets have provided unique ecohydrological insights-including dynamic root water uptake profiles, water age and storage effects, and hydraulic redistribution-and substantially improved the performance of site-scale soil–vegetation–atmosphere transfer (SVAT) and soil–plant–atmosphere continuum (SPAC) models, while noting that benefits for larger-scale climate models remain underexplored. We critically assess five persistent challenges: technical complexity and costs, reliable measurement at natural isotopic abundance, organic contamination and spectral interference, and ambiguity about the water pools sampled by different methods. We argue that carefully implemented in situ methods, supported by standardized calibration and post-processing workflows, explicit tests of isotopic equilibrium, and robust diagnosis and mitigation of organic contamination (e.g., micro-combustion modules), provide the most internally consistent means of linking soil and plant water isotope signals. Finally, we outline priorities for the community-including open processing protocols, coordinated long-term datasets, and closer collaboration with modelers-and recommend wider adoption of in sit

papers.title: GDDRP-CMIP6: Global Daily Runoff Projections from Bias-Corrected and Downscaled CMIP6 Forcing
papers.summary: Global runoff projections are essential for climate-change impact assessment, yet the native runoff of CMIP6 global climate models (GCMs) is spatially coarse, biased, and generated by heterogeneous land-surface schemes across models, limiting its further hydrological applications. Here we present the Global Daily Downscaled Runoff Projections CMIP6 (GDDRP-CMIP6), a global daily runoff ensemble dataset at 0.25° covering 1950–2100, generated within a unified modelling framework by driving the calibrated Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) model with bias-corrected and downscaled atmospheric forcings from NEX-GDDP-CMIP6. The dataset incorporates runoff of nine GCMs under the historical experiment and four SSP scenarios, whose transient climate response covers most of the very likely range assessed in the IPCC AR6. The simulated runoff, comprising surface runoff and baseflow, is routed through the global hydrodynamic model, CaMa-Flood, and evaluated against daily observations at 2,732 GRDC stations. The derived discharge reproduces the observed seasonal cycle with a global median climatological correlation of 0.83 and shows moderate median biases in mean, high, and low flows (−5.76 %, −10.18 %, and +10.65 %). Benchmarking against the native GCM runoff and against VIC simulations driven by raw CMIP6 forcings shows that bias correction generally improves agreement with observed discharge and reduces the median inter-member spread of the historical discharge climatology by about one order of magnitude. The inter-member range of projected discharge changes is also narrowed, mainly by the common hydrological model, while the ensemble-mean projected changes are broadly consistent with those of the native GCM runoff. By providing daily total runoff from 1950 to 2100 under four SSPs within a single globally consistent framework, including many islands absent from native GCM land masks, GDDRP-CMIP6 enables directly comparable flood, drought, and water-resource assessments acros

papers.title: Editorial: Integrating science and policy for water-sensitive urban planning in climate-impacted cities
papers.summary: converge on the same urban systems, making them more vulnerable to the rising impacts of climate change (IPCC, 2022;Hossain and Huq, 2013). While integrated, interdisciplinary planning for urban water is gaining momentum in policy, in practice it is still treated as a downstream technical service rather than as an organising principle of urban development, despite arguments that it should be the cross-cutting axis around which planning is organised (PolyUrbanWaters, 2026).Urban water research demands more integrated framing, and the integration of actors across the whole value chain, so that research translates into practice and establishes a feedback loop of continuous, evidence-driven planning and learning. Research on these coupled challenges remains largely supply-driven, is rarely interdisciplinary enough to match the problems it addresses, and is seldom brokered into the forms and moments in which planning decisions are taken, a difficulty researchers themselves attribute partly to weak institutional support for policy engagement (Lewis et al., 2022). This also requires the standardisation of approaches, frameworks and shared understanding towards the common goal of resilience in urban planning (Abeling et al., 2020). This Research Topic was convened to strengthen evidence-driven policymaking for resilient cities, with urban water placed at the core of the planning philosophy rather than at its margins.The five studies span four continents and much of the urban water cycle, across the Topic's themes: predictive modelling, data-driven governance, coastal interdependence, stakeholder collaboration and adaptation.The translation from analysis into decision is clearest in modelling. In Fast urban inundation simulation with RIM2D for flood risk assessment and forecasting, Apel et al. confront a practical barrier to impact-based warning: conventional coupled surface-sewer models are too data-hungry and slow for the cities that most need them. Their GPU-accelerated m

papers.title: High-resolution soil moisture reconstruction for Switzerland in 2016–2023
papers.summary: Soil moisture is a key environmental variable for hydrological processes, land-atmosphere interactions, vegetation water stress, and mass movements, yet it remains poorly known at high spatiotemporal resolution, even in well-instrumented areas. We present a high-resolution soil moisture reconstruction dataset for Switzerland (CH-SMR), consisting of daily maps at six depth levels from 0 to 2 m, at 250 m resolution, for 2016–2023. CH-SMR is generated with the Tethys-Chloris (T&C) land surface model, which simulates coupled water, carbon and energy balances at hourly time steps in a distributed framework. The reconstructed estimates agree well with in situ soil moisture measurements and outperform the ERA5-Land climate reanalysis, particularly during summer droughts. CH-SMR provides a basis for both scientific investigation and applied analysis by enabling the study of soil moisture variability and its impact on the response of forests, wetlands, and agricultural land. Potential applications include hydrological and ecological research, as well as drought and flood assessment, analyses of landslide hazard and vegetation water stress.

papers.title: Hydro-Thermal Performance and Evaporative Cooling Efficiency of Pervious Concrete Pavers Incorporating Recycled Seashell Aggregates
papers.summary: Pervious concrete pavements offer multifunctional urban benefits by mitigating stormwater runoff and providing evaporative surface cooling. Incorporating recycled aggregates into these systems further enhances sustainability by supporting circular-economy initiatives, through the recovery of seashells as construction aggregates and reduced demand for virgin mineral resources. This study investigates the influence of recycled seashell aggregates on pervious concrete pavers by comparing a baseline control formulation with a seashell-based mixture. A unified experimental framework was utilized to assess physical and mechanical properties, hydraulic performance, thermo-physical parameters, and surface thermal responses under controlled dry–wet testing with repeatable radiative forcing. The seashell-based formulation exhibited a 72% increase in open porosity and a 137% increase in measured infiltration rate, enhancing hydraulic functionality. This increase in open porosity was accompanied by a mechanical trade-off, reducing compressive strength to 4.44 MPa (38% of control), alongside a 43% decrease in thermal conductivity. During dry thermal testing, seashell pavers cooled faster at night (up to 5 °C lower). In wet testing, SPCP showed an average water-loss rate of 4.81 g/h over the first three days and daytime surface temperature reductions up to 7 °C and nighttime reductions up to 4 °C. Overall, recycled seashell aggregates enhance infiltration and evaporative cooling performance at the expense of structural capacity, supporting their potential for stormwater management and heat mitigation, subject to mechanical and durability validation for the intended application.

papers.title: Water Productivity Assessment Framework for Aquaculture Pond Systems: Physical, Nutritional, and Economic Dimensions
papers.source: CGSPace A Repository of Agricultural Research Outputs (Consultative Group for International Agricultural Research)
authors: W. W. M. Apsara P. K. Wanasinghe
papers.summary: Aquaculture water productivity is often assessed primarily in terms of fish yield per unit of water, with less attention given to the nutritional and economic value generated. To address this gap, this report introduces the Water Productivity Assessment Framework (WPAF), a methodological approach for assessing water productivity in closed aquaculture ponds across three complementary dimensions: physical water productivity (fish yield per cubic metre of water), nutritional water productivity (protein, fat, energy and selected micronutrients per cubic metre) and economic water productivity (gross and net returns per cubic metre). Each indicator is assessed against total water use and consumptive water use, accounting for evaporation, seepage and water retained in harvested fish. The framework combines household survey data and pond-level measurements with normative reference values for seepage, runoff coefficients and fish nutrient composition, while satellite-based energy-balance models are used to estimate evaporation. It provides a structured methodology specifying variables, equations, data requirements and sampling procedures to enable consistent assessments and comparisons across ponds, species combinations and management practices. Field validation is planned in 30–35 ponds in the Indian Sundarbans. While intended for closed aquaculture systems, the framework offers potential for wider application, subject to validation and adaptation to local agroecological conditions.

papers.title: Comment les pratiques et infrastructures agroécologiques améliorent la disponibilité en eau des agroécosystèmes ?
papers.summary: Water availability is a major limiting factor for the productivity and stability of agroecosystems in a context of increasing climate variability. Agroecology proposes five action levers: improving the use efficiency of rainfall and irrigation water, enhancing soil infiltration and storage, increasing root exploration volume, and reducing losses through runoff, evaporation, and drainage. This article synthesizes the quantitative effects of agroecological practices and infrastructures on the soil–plant–atmosphere water balance. While agroecological practices (no-till farming, mulching, cover crops, long and diversified crop rotations, agroforestry) and landscape infrastructures (hedgerows, grass strips, terraces, wetlands) generally improve water conservation and system resilience, their effectiveness remains highly dependent on climatic conditions, soil types, and spatial scales of implementation. The study also highlights antagonistic effects, particularly in intercropping systems where interspecific water competition can complicate flux management. Water availability therefore results from dynamic, multi-scale interactions between practices, soil, and climate.

GEOPHYSICAL INVESTIGATION AND SUBSURFACE HYDROGEOLOGICAL CHARACTERIZATION USING VERTICAL ELECTRICAL SOUNDING (VES) TECHNIQUE: A CASE STUDY OF APETE AKUFO PHASE 1, AWOTAN-ASUNLE AREA OF IBADAN, SOUTH-WEST NIGERIA
papers.source: Journal of Biodiversity and Environmental Research
papers.summary: The significance geophysical investigation and subsurface hydrogeological characterization in determining the geoelectric layers and the corresponding variations of aquifer parameters, in estimating the depth to competent bedrock and aquifer units, delineating zones of leachate contamination and vulnerability to pollution cannot be overemphasized in environmental studies.This study was conducted around the Phase 1 of Apete-Akufo dumpsite environment, Ibadan, Southwestern Nigeria. The geophysical method adopted was Vertical Electrical Sounding (VES) using the Schlumberger electrode configuration across ten (10) VES stations with half-electrode spread length (AB/2) of 75m each. The acquired data were processed and interpreted Winresist software to delineate subsurface layers and evaluate groundwater-related parameters including aquifer thickness, overburden thickness, bedrock elevation and longitudinal conductance among others. The variations of the geoelectric parameters were carried on each location using both 2D/3D contouring technique with golden surfer software. The results revealed variations in the acquired geoelectric parameters across the study area. Topsoil resistivity ranged from 22.3 to 233.7Ωm, weathered-layer resistivity from 15.1 to 145.1Ωm, aquifer thickness from 3.2 to 29.0 m, and overburden thickness from 4.3 to 29.7m; consequently, delineating locations of comparably high and low groundwater yields and protections. Longitudinal conductance values range from 0.068 to 0.852 mhos, indicating poor to moderate protective capacity ranges from 10%, 20% and 70% respectively exhibiting poor, weak and moderate protective capacities with none exhibiting good to excellent protective capacities. These results suggest that groundwater protection varies across the study area, with 90% of the locations being more susceptible to contamination in varying proportions. The study confirms that VES is highly instrumental in evaluating subsurface conditions and groundwate

papers.title: Attribution of changes in hydrological extremes in the eastern headwaters of the Asian water tower based on a causal discovery–machine learning–spatial heterogeneity attribution framework
papers.summary: Global change has profoundly altered hydrological regimes in the river-source basins of the eastern Tibetan Plateau, a core component of the Asian Water Tower. While previous studies have extensively documented changes in annual and monthly runoff, systematic attribution of hydrological extreme indices and their multi-factor driving mechanisms remains critically underexplored. To address this gap, we integrated runoff records from 102 gauging stations across two periods, earlier (1964–1979, period 1) and later (2006–2020, period 2), computed 62 hydrological extreme indices, and compiled explanatory variables covering extreme climate, landscape patterns, topography, vegetation, land use, and socioeconomic conditions. A three-tier framework was applied, combining temporal causal discovery (J-PCMCI+), machine-learning attribution (XGBoost-SHAP, RF, BRT), and spatial heterogeneity decomposition (OMGD), enabling systematic comparisons across all catchments as well as separately for natural and managed. The major conclusions are as follows: (1) In terms of multi-year averages, overall, runoff and most extreme indices are higher in period 1 than in period 2, while the change rate shows the opposite pattern. Yet with pronounced spatial disparities across the SYAR, SYER, and SIR basins, particularly for magnitude- and frequency-based indices, including mean and change rate. (2) Extreme climate indices exhibited strong spatial explanatory power but weak temporal predictability, with their effects substantially moderated by underlying surface conditions. In natural catchments, runoff was governed by a synergistic “climate–structure” control, where key climate indices coordinated with landscape metrics (COHESION, PD, DRD). In managed catchments, however, drivers shifted toward land use, water regulation, and ecological status, with SPI, NDVI, Water, Barren, NPP, pH, and Rwidth outweighing climatic factors. High-flow indices depended more on extreme precipitation and routing str

papers.title: Landslide directionality reveals fault-influenced valley-slope geometry in the northern Xiaojiang Fault Zone
papers.summary: Regional landslide inventories commonly describe where landslides occur, but they rarely capture the directional organization of slope failure. We compiled a remote-sensing-derived geomorphic inventory with 3,442 landslides along the northern Xiaojiang Fault Zone, southeastern Tibetan Plateau, and defined the principal runout direction as the plan-view vector from the highest point along the rear boundary to the centroid of each landslide polygon. Circular statistics, fault-distance zoning and the angle between landslide direction and local fault strike (ΔF) were used to evaluate regional landslide directional patterns. Landslide directions show a clear multimodal distribution, dominated by east-southeast and west-southwest sectors. Directional concentration varies spatially, with the lowest value in the 0–1 km fault-distance zone (0.1149) and the highest value beyond 5 km (0.3898). ΔF is strongly concentrated at high angles, indicating that the principal direction vectors are not parallel to the fault. Instead, their directions are more consistent with local valley–slope geometry that may result from the combined effects of prolonged fault activity and fluvial downcutting. Principal runout direction therefore provides information complementary to conventional inventory metrics and offers a regional-scale indicator for examining tectonic–geomorphic organization in active-fault mountain landscapes.

Research on temperature damage and control measures of high railway foundation with wind-deposited sand improved by cement
papers.summary: Aeolian sand is a common material in desert area. The use of cement-modified Aeolian sand as high railway foundation filling can reduce the construction cost, and its temperature effect is significantly affected by temperature, which seriously affects the performance safety of roadbed. In order to reveal the deformation and failure mechanism of high railway foundation under the action of temperature stress and improve the service life of roadbed, this paper adopts ANSYS numerical simulation method to study the deformation and failure mechanism of high railway foundation under the action of temperature stress on the basis of field investigation and test. A hexahedral eight-node isoparametric solid element suitable for the analysis of temperature field and temperature stress field of improved soil was selected, and the Ansys was used to establish the finite element model of cement improved eolus sand roadbed. A cement modified eolian sand high railway foundation model is constructed according to the actual project. The geometric model of the roadbed including the foundation bed and the bottom of the foundation bed is established according to the description in the project summary. The fatigue life of the roadbed is extended from 84.04 years to 113.72 years by presetting the expansion joint of the roadbed, and the life of the roadbed is increased by 35.3%, which meets the requirements of the design service life of the main engineering of the high-speed railway roadbed. The research results can provide a scientific reference for the design and maintenance of high railway foundation.

papers.title: Internal wetting responses of floodplain highway embankments under transient flood boundaries: Cross-scale simulation and service-stage effects
Thermo-hydro coupling characteristics and evolutionary interpretation of the “Crust-Loose-Base” ternary structure in arid earthen sites
papers.summary: Under climate change, surface weathering of arid earthen sites often leads to the formation of a characteristic “Crust-Loose-Base” layered structure, yet its thermo-hydro mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the transport properties and pore characteristics of different layers through moisture adsorption–desorption experiments, thermophysical measurements, and microstructural analyses. Results demonstrate that the Loose layer promotes liquid water infiltration and moisture retention, the Base layer facilitates capillary redistribution, while the Crust layer restricts liquid water penetration but allows vapor exchange. Differences in pore architecture, rather than mineral composition, primarily control these transport behaviors. Under thermal gradients, suction variations, and wetting–drying cycles, moisture redistribution may drive water accumulation in the Loose layer and crust formation at the surface. These findings advance the understanding of thermo-hydro coupling mechanisms governing layered structure evolution in arid earthen sites.

papers.title: A Review on Climate-Resilient Rainwater Management Systems for Island Agro-Ecosystems: Insights from the Andaman Islands
papers.summary: The Andaman archipelago presents an acute hydro-climatic conundrum. Annual rainfall is quite high(>3,000 mm) throughout a long monsoon season, but there are severe agricultural droughts andmoisture deficiencies between the months of January to April. The islands’ steep and undulatingtopography, small coastal valleys and tight geological strata dominated by shattered Andaman Flyschand ophiolite suites severely constrain regional groundwater storage, with more than 80% ofprecipitation emptying fast into the sea as runoff. Therefore, the regional agriculture has been limitedto a monsoon-driven single-crop paddy cycle followed by dry season fallow and root zone salinizationin low lying coastal regions. Pioneering research conducted by the Central Agricultural ResearchInstitute (ICAR-CARI, now CIARI) in Port Blair has addressed this paradox through landconfiguration engineering, micro-catchment harvesting, and integrated farming architectures. Thispaper analyzes the operational hydraulics, soil salinity abatement, and agronomic productivity ofCARI-developed technologies. The investigation examines both in-situ and ex-situ conservationstrategies suitable for the islands' vulnerable ecosystems. The Broad Bed and Furrow (BBF) systemof the low-lying seasonally inundated valley floors is a dual-purpose intervention. Raised beds providefree drainage for high value vegetable crops during torrential rains, while depressed furrows act aswater reservoirs for integrated paddy-cum-pisciculture and subsequent dry season irrigation. In themid-slope and highland plantation areas, the ex-situ rainwater gathering using dugout farm ponds andcheck dams traps the crucial surface runoff. Critical civil engineering countermeasures such asinstallation of UV stabilized 500-micron high density polyethylene (HDPE) liners to arrest heavylateral seepage through fractured subgrades and hydraulic design of stone pitched emergencyspillways capable of discharging cyclonic cloud bursts are studied. Analysis the Characteristics and Performance of Polyethersulfone-Carbon Nanotube Membranes Fabricated Using Electric Field Method for Water Filtration Applications
papers.summary: This study aims to address the effect of Carbon Nanotube (CNT) addition on the characteristics and performance of polyethersulfone (PES) membranes fabricated using the Electric Field method. Four PES membranes were fabricated with addition of CNT and denoted as SM0 (0% CNT), SM1 (0.5% CNT), SM2 (1% CNT), and SM3 (1.5% CNT). SEM observations showed average pore sizes of 0.62±0.12 μm to 0.82±0.18 μm, and AFM images showed the ability of CNTs to increase topographical complexity. The tensile test results indicated that addition of CNT increased the tensile strength of the membrane. The TGA and DTG test graphs showed that addition of CNT can increase the thermal resistance of the membrane. FTIR spectra were in agreement with characteristic PES functional groups. The XRD data showed that the amorphous nature remains dominant, indicating that this composite membrane successfully combines the mechanical strength and functional properties of CNTs without sacrificing the intrinsic pore structure of the PES polymer. Addition of CNT to the membrane increased its hydrophilicity, as evidenced by decrease in water contact angle on the membrane. Addition of CNT can also increase the membrane permeability, as indicated by an increase in the membrane permeability values in the range of 1 to 6 bar. In terms of durability, adding CNT to the membrane can increase its durability, meaning that membranes with added CNT can last longer than pure PES membranes.
