papers.title: Development of an AI-Driven Model to Predict Slope Collapse Due to Rainfall
papers.summary: Rainfall-induced slope instability is one of the most critical geotechnical hazards worldwide, causing significant damage to infrastructure and loss of life. Predicting slope stability under rainfall conditions remains challenging due to the complex interaction between soil properties, slope geometry, and transient hydrological processes. This research addresses this challenge by developing a reliable and practical predictive framework that integrates experimental investigation, numerical modeling, and machine learning. The study was conducted in three sequential stages. First, geotechnical centrifuge tests were performed at the University of Western Ontario to investigate slope response under controlled rainfall conditions. A calibrated rainfall simulation system ensured uniform and repeatable rainfall application, while slope deformation and pore water pressures were monitored to understand failure mechanisms. Second, numerical simulations using SEEP/W and SLOPE/W were conducted to evaluate slope stability across a wide range of conditions, including different soil types (clay, silt, and sand), slope geometries, and rainfall scenarios. This process generated a comprehensive dataset of 21,438 cases. Finally, machine learning models, including Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Extra Trees, were developed to predict the factor of safety using seven input variables. The Extra Trees model showed the highest predictive accuracy and strong generalization capability, particularly under unseen slope geometries. The results also highlight the importance of including rainfall intensity and duration in predictive models. The developed model was implemented into a web-based early warning system capable of providing rapid predictions. This research contributes to improved hazard assessment and supports the development of practical tools for geotechnical risk mitigation.

papers.title: Base-level lowering rates control a landslide process transition in California's Franciscan mélange
papers.summary: California’s Franciscan mélange is well-known for hosting persistent, slow-moving earthflows, a landslide style favored by the unit’s significant local variability in shear strength (e.g. Medley, 2001; Kim et al., 2004; Roering et al., 2015). Big Sur’s mélange, however, is unusual: landslide mapping there reveals both recent (e.g. the 2017 Mud Creek landslide) and prehistoric rotational landslides on slopes that are unusually steep for this lithology. Because rotational landslides and earthflows pose markedly different hazards, understanding what drives the shift in failure style is critical for hazard assessment. Here we test the hypothesis that the rate of base-level lowering governs the transition between earthflow and rotational failure. We synthesize landslide mapping and analysis of high-resolution topography across two Franciscan mélange settings with contrasting rates of base-level lowering: the South Fork Eel River canyon, where river incision drives base-level lowering at ~1 mm/yr, and the southern Big Sur coast, where wave erosion drives local base-level lowering at ~2 cm/yr. We then use 2-D numerical modeling to test whether rapid coastal retreat alone can drive a transition from earthflow to rotational failure in a Franciscan mélange hillslope.Landslide mapping shows that landslide activity in Big Sur, as defined by InSAR-derived deformation rates, is concentrated along the actively eroding coastline, and that the two regions differ systematically in failure style according to overall hillslope angle. Big Sur’s steeper slopes are dominated by rotational landslides, while the Eel River region’s shallower slopes are dominated by earthflows. Numerical modeling shows that progressive lateral erosion can produce rotational failure on hillslopes that were previously deforming as earthflows, provided there is some degree of vertical heterogeneity in the weathering profile. papers.title: Digital soil mapping of mountain soils: from pedodiversity to land vocation and ecosystem services
papers.source: AMS Dottorato Institutional Doctoral Theses Repository (University of Bologna)
papers.summary: This doctoral research explored the application of Geographic Information System (GIS) and Digital Soil Mapping (DSM) techniques to improve soil mapping processes and support land management and biodiversity conservation, in alignment with the objectives of the National Biodiversity Future Center (NBFC). The study was conducted in two Regional Parks of the Northern Apennines, a region characterized by high environmental heterogeneity and a rich cartographic heritage. Traditional pedological knowledge and expert-driven selection of environmental covariates were first employed to delineate land units and produce a conventional soil map. Subsequently, DSM approaches using Random Forest models with recursive feature elimination were applied to generate an alternative soil map based on DEM derivatives and remotely sensed data, achieving high accuracy and interpretability. The analysis identified key drivers of soil differentiation, such as topography, insolation, vegetation indices, and proximity to water bodies, highlighting their potential for transferability to similar areas and for overcoming cartographic discontinuities. Complementary studies on the same area revealed that climate exerts a stronger influence than vegetation on soil evolution, and that considering soil diversity enhances understanding of organic matter dynamics. The second component of this research addressed the reestablishment of chestnut cultivation in the Northern Apennines through a land suitability model that was tested on the municipality of Castel del Rio (BO). The resulting map identified both underutilized suitable lands and cultivated areas with significant limitations, findings that were corroborated by the severe landslides of May 2023. Moreover, the study suggested that land morphology and soil characteristics may influence the spread of ink disease, a major threat to chestnut groves. papers.title: Analisis Kerawanan Longsorlahan di Kabupaten Wonogiri Berdasarkan Sistem Informasi Geografis
papers.source: UMS Library Center of Academic Activities (Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta)
authors: , Dr. Annisa Trisnia Sasmi, S.Si., M.T
papers.summary: Landslides are processes involving the downslope movement of soil and/or rock masses due to slope instability. Wonogiri Regency exhibits diverse topographic, rainfall, geological, land-use, and soil characteristics, resulting in varying levels of landslide susceptibility across the region. This study aims to analyze the spatial distribution of landslide susceptibility levels and their correspondence with actual landslide occurrences in Wonogiri Regency. A quantitative method was employed using a Geographic Information System (GIS) approach via the Weighted Overlay method. The parameters utilized included rainfall, slope gradient, geology, land use, and soil type. Each parameter was assigned a score and weight, followed by an overlay process to generate a landslide susceptibility map. Validation was conducted using 85 landslide occurrence points from 2025, obtained from the Wonogiri Regency Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD), with 12 of these points verified through field surveys. The results indicate that landslide susceptibility is categorized into four classes: low, moderate, high, and very high. The moderate susceptibility class covers the largest area. Validation results show that 57 occurrence points (67.06%) fall within the high susceptibility class, while 28 points (32.94%) fall within the moderate susceptibility class; no occurrence points were found in the low susceptibility class. These findings demonstrate that actual landslides occurred more frequently in areas classified as having high susceptibility compared to those with moderate susceptibility.

papers.title: EVALUASI KESESUAIAN RENCANA TATA RUANG WILAYAH BERBASIS PEMETAAN TINGKAT BAHAYA LONGSOR MENGGUNAKAN SISTEM INFORMASI GEOGRAFIS DI KECAMATAN COBLONG KOTA BANDUNG
papers.source: Repository at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia (Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia)
papers.summary: Kecamatan Coblong merupakan salah satu wilayah perkotaan di Kota Bandung yang memiliki kondisi lereng bervariasi serta tekanan pemanfaatan ruang yang cukup tinggi, sehingga berpotensi mengalami bencana tanah longsor. Perkembangan pembangunan pada kawasan lereng menuntut adanya kajian spasial yang mampu mengidentifikasi tingkat bahaya longsor sekaligus meninjau kesesuaiannya terhadap arahan Rencana Tata Ruang Wilayah (RTRW). Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk memetakan tingkat bahaya tanah longsor serta menganalisis keterkaitannya dengan pola ruang RTRW menggunakan pendekatan Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG). Metode kerja yang digunakan mengadopsi teknik skoring dan pembobotan multiparameter yang merujuk pada regulasi standar nasional Permen PU No. 22/PRT/M/2007. Adapun variabel spasial yang diintegrasikan mencakup aspek fisik lingkungan, antara lain kemiringan lereng (ekstraksi data DEM), data curah hujan, pedologi (jenis tanah), litologi (jenis batuan), serta dinamika tutupan lahan. Seluruh layer data tersebut dikonversi ke dalam format vektor untuk diproses menggunakan teknik spatial overlay dengan metode Intersect, guna menghasilkan unit analisis baru yang merepresentasikan indeks bahaya. Hasil penelitian menghasilkan peta distribusi spasial bahaya tanah longsor di Kecamatan Coblong yang bervariasi dan terbagi menjadi tiga kelas diantaranya rendah, sedang, dan tinggi dengan kelas bahaya sedang sebagai yang terluas. Hasil pengolahan peta zona tipologi membagi kedalam tiga zona yaitu zona A, B, dan C dan zona tipologi C sebagai zona yang paling mendominasi di lokasi penelitian. Analisis kesesuaian terhadap RTRW terbagi kedalam beberapa kategori diantaranya, kategori sesuai, sesuai bersyarat yang merupakan kategori terluas pada lokasi penelitian, dan tidak sesuai, sementara kategori lainnya berperan dalam menjaga keseimbangan lingkungan. Peta tematik yang dihasilkan diharapkan dapat menjadi informasi pendukung dalam pengendalian pemanfaatan ruang serta perencanaan wilay

papers.title: INTEGRASI PERSISTENT SCATTERER INTERFEROMETRIC SYNTHETIC APERTURE RADAR (PS-INSAR) DAN ANALYTICAL HIERARCHY PROCESS (AHP) UNTUK PEMETAAN KERAWANAN LONGSOR DI SEKITAR LAPANGAN PANAS BUMI WAYANG WINDU
papers.source: Repository at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia (Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia)
papers.summary: Kawasan Panas Bumi Wayang Windu merupakan wilayah yang memiliki potensi tanah longsor yang tinggi. Pemetaan kerawanan longsor umumnya masih menggunakan parameter statis sehingga belum sepenuhnya merepresentasikan kondisi pergerakan permukaan tanah secara aktual. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan mengintegrasikan informasi deformasi permukaan hasil PS-InSAR ke dalam metode Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) untuk pemetaan kerawanan longsor serta mengevaluasi tingkat akurasi hasil pemetaan di sekitar Lapangan Panas Bumi Wayang Windu. Penelitian memanfaatkan 60 citra Sentinel-1A periode 2024–2026, serta beberapa parameter kerawanan longsor lainnya seperti kemiringan lereng, curah hujan, penggunaan lahan, jenis tanah, jenis batuan, dan jarak dari patahan. Pembobotan parameter dilakukan menggunakan AHP berdasarkan penilaian ahli, kemudian seluruh parameter diintegrasikan melalui analisis weighted overlay. Hasil pengolahan PS-InSAR menunjukkan deformasi Line of Sight (LOS) berkisar antara -33 hingga 38 mm/tahun yang menunjukkan adanya fenomena subsidence dan uplift. Integrasi deformasi permukaan ke dalam model AHP menghasilkan peta kerawanan longsor empat kelas, yaitu rendah, sedang, tinggi, dan sangat tinggi. Hasil validasi menggunakan matriks konfusi menunjukkan nilai Overall Accuracy sebesar 95,4% dan koefisien Kappa sebesar 93,4%, yang menunjukkan bahwa integrasi PS-InSAR dan AHP mampu menghasilkan pemetaan kerawanan longsor dengan tingkat ketelitian yang baik serta dapat mendukung upaya mitigasi bencana di sekitar Panas Bumi Wayang Windu. The Wayang Windu Geothermal Field is an area with a high potential for landslides. Landslide susceptibility mapping generally relies on static parameters, which do not fully represent actual ground surface movement. papers.title: Advances in the detection and monitoring of mass-movement processes through high-resolution remote sensing data
papers.summary: With advances in satellite technology, spaceborne data are becoming available to the public and scientific community at increasing temporal and spatial resolutions. These data open new opportunities to study Earth-surface processes in unprecedented detail. This thesis investigates the potential and challenges of high-resolution optical data for monitoring slow-moving landslides and the generation of digital elevation models (DEMs) to improve subsequent topographic analyses. The study area is set in the northwest Argentinean Andes -- a region particularly susceptible to mass movement processes due to steep topography, heavy rainfall during the summer monsoon, and geologic pre-conditioning. To obtain a more detailed reconstruction of local topography, tri-stereo SPOT-7 data were used to infer a 3-m DEM of the intermontane Quebrada del Toro basin through stereophotogrammetry. GNSS field measurements were employed to validate the derived elevations and identify optimal processing parameters. In steep mountain terrain, where global radar-derived DEMs frequently suffer from layover and shadowing effects, high-resolution stereo data can help to reduce artifacts and better resolve the traces of channelized processes. The longitudinal channel profiles extracted from the 3-m DEM contain topographic signatures of both fluvial erosion and debris flows, which are based on the relationship between slope and drainage area. Debris-flow activity is presumed to dominate in channels that exhibit minimal curvature despite an increase in drainage areas. The topographic signature of debris-flow activity is found throughout the Toro basin, fueled by pervasively fractured bedrock along the major bounding fault systems. Mass-movement processes are also common in the neighboring Quebrada de Humahuaca basin. papers.title: Assessing the influence of rainfall-induced desiccation cracking on slope stability in Malaysia
papers.summary: The influence of climate change on slope stability has become increasingly relevant in recent years, particularly in tropical regions like Malaysia, where the frequency and severity of rainfall events are anticipated to vary considerably. This study examined the combined impacts of rainfall variability and soil desiccation cracking on the slope stability in Malaysia’s tropical granitic residual soils. The study conducted a comprehensive analysis of precipitation patterns utilizing both historical and projected climatic data across multiple climate change scenarios. It subsequently investigated the formation of desiccation cracks in soils exposed to repeated cycles of wetting and drying under controlled laboratory circumstances, replicating actual seasonal variations. Numerical models evaluated the impact of rainfall infiltration on slope stability amid changing climatic circumstances. The rainfall pattern analysis revealed a notable tendency of increasing wet-season rainfall but a considerable decline in dry-season precipitation. This extreme climate condition has provoked the formation of desiccation cracks on soil slopes. The subsequent experimental study indicated that desiccation cracks substantially enhance water infiltration into the soil. The mechanism involved increased crack formation with the repetitive wetting-drying cycles, leading to increased void ratio in soil, and hence resulted in a higher permeability. The numerical analysis reported that slopes with gentler gradients exhibited less sensitivity to climate change impact, with average Factor of Safety (FOS) values of about 0.8, 0.95, and 1.1 for slopes of 1V:1H, 1V:1.5H, and 1V:2H, respectively, under future rainfall conditions. From 2024 to 2070, the percentage of time during which FOS fell below 1.0 was 91.4%, 70.1%, and 35.3% for these three slope gradients under the MIROC5_RCP8.5 scenario (and 90.5%, 67.4%, and 27.3% under MIROC5_RCP4.5), indicating a substantial reduction in stability. papers.title: Multi-hazard modelling of hydro-geomorphological events for early warning systems. Application to the Val d’Aran (Central Pyrenees, Spain)
papers.source: UPCommons institutional repository (Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya)
papers.summary: (English) Hydro-geomorphological hazards such as floods and rainfall-induced landslides frequently co-occur in mountainous regions, driven by shared meteorological forcing but governed by distinct hydrological and geotechnical mechanisms. Improving their anticipation requires modelling frameworks capable of consistently representing subsurface hydrological conditioning and its interaction with transient triggering processes. This thesis develops and evaluates a physically based, forecast-driven multi-hazard modelling framework for early warning applications in the Upper Garonne River Basin (Val d’Aran, Central Pyrenees, Spain). The research progresses through three interconnected stages. First, an event-based slope stability model is enhanced through a novel multi-objective calibration strategy that explicitly represents both antecedent and final slope stability conditions. Results demonstrate that inadequate representation of subsurface hydrological states leads to physically inconsistent pre-event instability, highlighting the sensitivity of slope response to antecedent moisture conditions. Building on this finding, a continuous distributed hydrological–geotechnical modelling system (SCLAM) is developed to dynamically simulate snowmelt, rainfall–runoff processes, groundwater redistribution, and slope stability within a unified framework. By replacing externally imposed antecedent conditions with internally simulated hydrological states, the model improves physical consistency and identifies Baseflow Excess as a main indicator of destabilizing subsurface conditions. The coupled framework is subsequently extended into a prototype multi-hazard early warning system integrating flood and landslide forecasting under bias-corrected ensemble meteorological forcings. papers.title: Engineering geological properties of the Awhitu Group sands at Muriwai, New Zealand
papers.summary: Landslides are a critical risk to New Zealand’s infrastructure and economy, as evidenced during the widespread early 2023 storms. The Awhitu Group sands are late Pliocene to early Pleistocene dune sands and associated facies found throughout the New Zealand North Island west coast. Muriwai, a settlement in the Auckland region, has an 80 m escarpment consisting of Awhitu Group sands that failed as fatal landslides during strong rainfall in early 2023 and in 1965. Interestingly, there is currently limited research on the geotechnical properties of the Awhitu Group sands, particularly at Muriwai. Therefore, this study aims to develop a more comprehensive understanding of the engineering geology properties of the Muriwai Awhitu Group sands to gain more appreciation for the complexity of this geological unit and the Muriwai slope conditions. Awhitu Group sands at or near the 2023 Muriwai landslide areas were sampled and tested in-situ with a shear vane and handheld penetrometer. Subsequently, laboratory work was conducted on the Muriwai Awhitu Group sand samples such as particle size analysis, Atterberg limits and linear shrinkage tests, dispersion experiments, X-Ray Fluorescence analysis, Scanning Electron Microscope and Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy investigations, as well direct shear tests. Additionally, digital ArcGIS examinations were undertaken to assess the dimensions and pre-failure topography of the 2023 Muriwai landslide areas. The Muriwai Awhitu Group sand samples were found to be predominantly poorly graded very fine to medium sands that have some low plasticity active clays. The samples were mostly composed of quartz, aluminosilicates (including feldspars, smectite, halloysite, allophane, kaolinite and illite), and some iron. Moreover, the samples were generally non-expansive, non-dispersive, moderately sensitive, stiff to hard, and moderately cemented with some high cohesion and internal friction angle values. papers.title: Engineering Geological Investigation of Rainfall Triggered Landslides in Tropical Volcanic-Sedimentary Residual Soils, Mont Robinson, New Caledonia
papers.summary: Intense rainfall events in the Mont Robinson region of New Caledonia frequently trigger shallow translational landslides on steep volcanic-sedimentary terrain. Despite the region's tropical climate, rugged topography, and recurring landslide activity, New Caledonia has been largely absent from global landslide inventory studies, creating a significant knowledge gap in the understanding of landslides occurring in tropical residual soils. This study investigates the geological, mineralogical, geotechnical, and hydrological controls governing slope failure in these weathered volcanic-sedimentary materials. Field investigations were undertaken to characterise landslide morphology and collect representative soil samples for laboratory testing. Physical, mineralogical, and geochemical analyses were combined with geotechnical characterisation and slope stability modelling using Factor of Safety (FoS) analyses to evaluate the mechanisms responsible for failure. This integrated approach enabled the relationships between weathering, soil composition, hydrological response, and slope stability to be examined. The results demonstrate that the clay mineral assemblage and degree of weathering exert a primary control on the engineering behaviour of the residual soils. The shallow, fine-grained weathered materials exhibit high rainfall sensitivity, with intense precipitation causing rapid infiltration, elevated pore-pressures, reduced effective stress, and a corresponding loss of shear strength. The resulting failures are characterised as shallow translational landslides controlled by rapid saturation, limited subsurface drainage, and accelerated strength degradation. Strong agreement between mineralogical, geotechnical, hydrological, and landslide inventory datasets confirms that material properties directly influence rainfall response and observed failure mechanisms. papers.title: Engineering Geological Investigation of Landslides on the Āwhitu Peninsula, Auckland, New Zealand
papers.summary: During January and February 2023, the Auckland region experienced three major storm events - ex-Tropical Cyclone Hale (10th January), the Auckland Anniversary Floods (27th January), and ex-Tropical Cyclone Gabrielle (12th-15th February). These events triggered widespread landsliding across the Āwhitu Peninsula, causing significant damage to critical road infrastructure. This study investigates the engineering geological characteristics of these rainfall-triggered landslides and identifies the key factors controlling slope failure. The investigation comprised (1) a preliminary desktop study and landslide inventory, (2) in- situ testing of slope materials, (3) laboratory analysis of soil index properties and mineralogy, and (4) slope stability modelling. The predominant landslide types were deep-seated rotational failures that transitioned into earthflows downslope, together with shallow translational failures. The slope materials consisted primarily of dune sands of the Āwhitu and Kariotahi Groups, with locally altered expressions of Kidnappers Tephra identified through mineralogical analysis. Laboratory testing indicated that the sediments exhibited low to non- plastic behaviour, low clay activity, and stable granular structures. Although predominantly granular, the materials displayed relatively high apparent cohesion under partially saturated conditions. Slope stability modelling demonstrated that progressively increasing groundwater levels reduced the factor of safety and increased the likelihood of slope failure. The cumulative effect of the severe storm events in early 2023 was identified as the primary trigger for landsliding across the Peninsula. papers.title: Thermo-hydro-mechanical modeling of unsaturated vegetated slopes
papers.source: UPCommons institutional repository (Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya)
papers.summary: (English) The top layer of soil on a slope is highly dynamic, influenced by atmospheric forces and the presence of vegetation. The vegetation condition plays a crucial role in determining the amount of water transpiration and evaporation from the slope surface, thus affecting slope performance by altering temperature, water content, and pore water pressure within the soil mass. Many numerical models often neglect the vegetation impact on soil performance. To capture these effects, this study employs a finite element model in CODE_BRIGHT that integrates vegetation and climate-driven interactions, aiming to bridge the gap between reality and simulation. A specialized boundary condition is developed to simulate soil–vegetation–atmosphere (SVA) processes with hydraulic hysteresis, linking canopy resistance to solar radiation, vapor pressure deficit, and soil saturation. Model validation using three years of field data from the Agropolis slope in Barcelona shows strong agreement, confirming its ability to reproduce vegetation effects on slope hydrothermal behavior. Results reveal pronounced daily temperature variations in the root zone, higher temperatures on south-facing slopes, and stronger drying under vegetation during hot, dry periods. Parametric analysis identifies leaf area index (LAI), root density, and vegetation fraction as key factors influencing soil moisture. Root density and LAI most strongly affect water retention, dense roots lower summer saturation by up to 40%, while high LAI reduces surface drying by 30%. Vegetation fraction enhances winter storage but intensifies summer drying. To better represent unsaturated soils, a hysteretic soil–water retention model is implemented in CODE_BRIGHT, coupling suction and void ratio changes to improve accuracy in scenarios such as rainfall-induced landslides. papers.title: Pemetaan Kerawanan Tanah Longsor di Desa Bonto Lojong Kecamatan Uluere Kabupaten Bantaeng dengan Metode Frequency Ratio
papers.summary: Background: Landslides are a natural disaster that often occurs in Indonesia, particularly in areas with steep slopes and high rainfall. Bonto Lojong Village in Uluere District, Bantaeng Regency, exhibits these characteristics, yet there is no landslide susceptibility map for the area. Aim: To map the level of landslide susceptibility in Bonto Lojong Village, Uluere District, Bantaeng Regency, as a basis for disaster mitigation. Methods: Landslide susceptibility mapping was performed using the frequency ratio method, landslide inventory with Google Earth Pro, soil texture analysis using the hydrometer method, c-organic analysis using the Walkley and Black method, soil permeability using the constant head method, and bulk density using the gravimetric method. Results: Landslide susceptibility maps were divided into three classes of susceptibility, namely low, medium, and high, which were influenced by slopes > 45%, sandy clay texture, medium permeability (5,2-6,3) cm/jam, medium bulk density (1,20-1,34 g/cm³), and low c-organic (1,73-1,84%). The low-vulnerability class had an area of 684 ha in the western part of the study, the medium-vulnerability class had an area of 1,047 ha in the central-eastern part, and the high-vulnerability class had an area of 224 ha in the northern-southern part. There were 44 landslide occurrence points in Bonto Lojong Village, with 20 landslide occurrence points in the high vulnerability class, with variations in fr ranging from 1.0-12.28, the medium vulnerability class had 18 occurrence points, whereas in the low vulnerability class, there were six landslide points. Conclusions: Landslide vulnerability mapping using the frequency ratio method can produce maps with a good level of accuracy (AUC = 0.80). papers.title: Assessment of sediment production, connectivity, and delivery in mountainous catchments under environmental changes. The role of shallow landslides in the Upper Llobregat Basin (Pre-Pyrenees, Catalonia)
papers.source: UPCommons institutional repository (Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya)
papers.summary: (English) Soil erosion in mountainous landscapes is strongly influenced by shallow landslides, particularly during extreme precipitation events. Despite their geomorphic significance, quantitative soil erosion studies often prioritize fine sediment dynamics and agricultural land-use calibrations, thereby underrepresenting the complexity of landslide processes driven by intrinsic slope parameters and external triggering forces. This study examines sediment production and connectivity from shallow landslides under climate change and land-cover transitions. The primary objective aims to quantify sediment mobilization from slope instabilities to fluvial networks, focusing on the Saldes River Basin (102 km²) for model calibration and applying the results to the Upper Llobregat River Basin (504 km²). The quantification approach used a distributed, event-based method with the FSLAM landslide stability model. Projected climate scenarios predict increased extreme precipitation events, resulting in heightened slope mass wasting. Future simulations indicate landslide mobilization rates increase by 10%, peaking at 16% during 20-year rainfall events. These findings underscore the significance of hillslope processes in sediment budget assessments and the role of extreme rainfall in sediment production. To address sediment connectivity, this study introduces the Random Connect (RC) model. The model uses a random-walk framework and applies the Index of Connectivity (IC) to estimate sediment volume fluxes from source areas to channel networks. The input data includes a digital elevation model, IC maps, and sediment source maps derived from shallow landslides. The model outputs consist of raster maps that describe sediment flux. The receive maps show accumulated sediment volumes along transfer paths, and the release maps indicate the source cells contributing sediment to the target river. papers.title: Landslide susceptibility assessment for the Nihotupu reservoir system applying machine learning algorithms under different sampling strategies and mapping units
papers.summary: This study developed a landslide susceptibility modelling framework for the Nihotupu reservoir system, located in the Waitākere Ranges, Auckland, New Zealand, to evaluate how different spatial representations of terrain influence model performance and susceptibility mapping. A landslide inventory derived from Auckland Council was used as the primary input for the analysis. For this dataset, a sampling strategy was designed based on landslide scarp centroids and source-area boundary points, complemented by random sampling of non-landslide locations across the study area. Following this procedure, a balanced database of landslide and non-landslide samples was constructed and combined with a set of conditioning factors representing topographic, hydrological, geological, anthropogenic, and rainfall-related variables. Three mapping unit scenarios were implemented: pixel-based, slope-unit-based, and 20 m buffer-based representations of the terrain. Based on these scenarios, a feature reduction was performed using Pearson correlation analysis, variance inflation factor (VIF) filtering, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) importance prior to model training. The resulting predictor sets were subsequently used to train three machine-learning algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Then, model performance was assessed under spatial cross-validation using standard classification metrics, including area under the ROC curve (AUC), F1-score, accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, and precision–recall AUC (Pr-AUC). The results indicate that SVM consistently delivered the strongest predictive performance across the three scenarios, achieving the highest AUC values in the pixel-based (0.853), slope-unit-based (0.794), and buffer-based (0.846) workflows, while RF remained highly competitive, particularly in the buffer scenario. papers.title: Numerical Modelling of Quick Clay Landslides using the Material Point Method
papers.summary: Ved å gjennomføre en tilbakeberegning av kvikkleireskredet i Gjerdrum i 2020, ble egenskapene til MPM-beregningsprogrammet Anura3D vurdert. Den endelige simuleringen av Gjerdrum skredet tok omtrent to dager å fullføre. Anura3D ble vurdert som tregt og ikke egnet for videre bruk til mer komplekse problemer. Det ble derfor valgt å utføre simuleringer av en idealisert skråning for å undersøke effekten av anisotrop skjærstyrke ved bruk av NGI-ADP soft. Resultatene viste at NGI-ADP soft ga en senere skråningskollaps enn når Tresca soft ble benyttet. Innføring av anisotropi førte også til raskere retrogressjon og større utløpshastighet. Til slutt ble resultatene fra simuleringene av den idealiserte skråningen sammenlignet med aktsomhetsområdet beskrevet i NVEs veileder «Sikkerhet mot kvikkleireskred». Det anbefales videre å benytte et MPM beregningsprogram som støtter HPC for å kunne analysere mer komplekse problemstillinger. Videre anbefales det å utføre flere simuleringer med anisotropi for å studere effektene nærmere, samt å undersøke en realistisk case for å kunne sammenligne resultatene bedre med gjeldende standarder for kartlegging av aktsomhetsområder.

papers.title: A framework for spatio-temporal assessment of slope stability along mountainous transport corridors
papers.summary: Globally, research on the interaction between roads and landslides has largely focused on roads as triggering factors. Existing susceptibility assessments typically represent roads through static conditioning factors such as distance to road or road density, while limited attention has been given to how road infrastructure itself responds to dynamic slope processes. Consequently, their outputs often lack practical relevance for infrastructure resilience, particularly under evolving climate and environmental conditions. The aim of this research is to develop a dynamic, spatio-temporal framework that integrates hydrological conditions with slope stability analysis to assess landslide susceptibility along transport corridors. The approach couples daily soil water balance with a modified version of the physically based Transient Rainfall Infiltration and Grid-Based Regional Slope-Stability (TRIGRS) model. The framework was applied to the 24.7 km long Mukamira'Kabaya road and its 16.8 km² surrounding corridor in northwestern Rwanda, a steep environment frequently affected by shallow rainfall-induced landslides. A tartan-style visualisation was developed to depict dynamic landslide susceptibility along the road, illustrating how instabilities originating from either roadcut or upslope zones influence specific 10 m-long road sections through time. The coupled hydrological'mechanical model captured the temporal response of slope stability to variable rainfall. As part of model validation, the framework was applied using 2016 rainfall data and corresponding landslide records. It identified pronounced peaks in the proportions of roadcut and upslope areas with FoS ' 1.0 on 8 May (day 129 of the year), reaching 64% and 16 %, respectively ' coinciding with well-documented landsliding events in the corridor. The model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.89, demonstrating strong performance. These results confirm that the coupled model provides a realistic representation o

papers.title: PENGARUH PERUBAHAN TUTUPAN LAHAN TERHADAP TINGKAT KERAWANAN TANAH LONGSOR DI KOTA CIMAHI
papers.source: Repository at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia (Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia)
papers.summary: Bencana tanah longsor merupakan salah satu bencana alam yang sering terjadi pada wilayah dengan topografi curam, curah hujan tinggi, serta perubahan tutupan lahan yang tidak terkendali. Kota Cimahi sebagai wilayah dengan morfologi perbukitan dan perkembangan pembangunan yang pesat memiliki potensi kerawanan tanah longsor yang tinggi. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis perubahan tutupan lahan di Kota Cimahi pada tahun 2024 dan 2026, mengkaji tingkat kerawanan tanah longsor di Kota Cimahi berdasarkan analisis parameter curah hujan, kemiringan lereng, jenis batuan, tutupan lahan, dan jenis tanah dengan menggunakan analisis Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG) melalui teknik scoring dan overlay, serta menganalisis pengaruh perubahan tutupan lahan terhadap tingkat kerawanan tanah longsor di Kota Cimahi. Metode yang digunakan adalah deskriptif kuantitatif dengan pendekatan Sistem Informasi Geografis (SIG) melalui teknik change detection serta teknik scoring dan overlay. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa terjadi perubahan tutupan lahan sebesar ±37,73 ha dengan peningkatan kawasan terbangun sebesar ±1.446,24 ha yang tersebar terutama pada wilayah dengan aktivitas perkotaan yang tinggi, sedangkan penurunan tutupan lahan terjadi pada vegetasi berupa sawah dan tegalan/ladang dengan total ±1.291,38 ha. Tingkat kerawanan tanah longsor terbagi menjadi beberapa kelas dari tidak rawan, agak rawan, rawan, dan sangat rawan, dengan dominasi pada wilayah berlereng curam dan curah hujan tinggi. Perubahan tingkat kerawanan terjadi pada beberapa wilayah, dengan peningkatan kerawanan terbesar ditemukan pada Kelurahan Cibeber sebesar 24,30 ha, Leuwigajah sebesar 4,88 ha, dan Cibeureum sebesar 3,93 ha. Hasil uji regresi linier juga menunjukkan bahwa perubahan tutupan lahan memberikan kontribusi sebesar 99,0% terhadap peningkatan tingkat kerawanan tanah longsor, sedangkan 1,0% lainnya dipengaruhi oleh faktor parameter lain. Hasil penelitian ini diharapkan dapat menjadi dasar dalam peren

papers.title: Characterizing Hydrophysical and Biogeochemical Alteration and DNA Recovery in Highly Compressed Peat under Access Road Disturbance in a Boreal Fen
papers.source: Libraries and Cultural Resources (University of Calgary)
papers.summary: Boreal peatlands store carbon and regulate hydrology because saturation slows decomposition and allows peat to accumulate. Roads interrupt these controls by compressing peat and blocking lateral groundwater flow, producing persistent changes in water-table position, oxygen exposure, solute movement, and decomposition. As road removal and peatland reclamation become more common, restoration must be guided by how disturbance continues to affect ecosystem function below ground, rather than only whether vegetation or surface hydrology appear to recover. The first aspect of this thesis examined how a mineral access road altered hydrophysical structure, peat compression, and chemistry across depth in a moderate-rich treed fen near Slave Lake, Alberta. Road loading compressed and displaced peat horizons, while reduced hydraulic conductivity beneath the road divided the site into wetter upgradient and drier downgradient zones. These hydrological contrasts were consistent with differences in nutrient transport, ionic conditions, and decomposition patterns. Because subsurface compression can persist after mineral fill is removed, restoration planning must address both lateral hydrological reconnection and the altered vertical arrangement of peat that controls water storage, redox conditions, and substrate availability. The second aspect of this thesis followed up on these findings by asking whether the same changes in peat structure and organic matter chemistry also affect molecular monitoring. DNA-based methods can identify microbial responses before visible ecosystem recovery, but only when extraction differences reflect biological conditions rather than peat chemistry. The study therefore evaluated how disturbance, depth, and humification influenced DNA yield and purity, and whether modified extraction protocols reduced the effects of nucleic acid binding and humic inhibitor carry-over. The road created a compressed, vertically reorganized peat profile in which depth no lo

papers.title: Effects of root architecture of different wheat cultivars on soil structure
papers.source: AMS Dottorato Institutional Doctoral Theses Repository (University of Bologna)
papers.summary: Plant roots play a crucial role in maintaining soil health by influencing physical structure and hydraulic properties. This study investigates relationships between root morphology of wheat genotypes and their impacts on soil structure and hydraulic characteristics. Using shovelomics, we characterized root systems of wheat cultivars (Paragon, Bologna) and landraces (Senatore-Cappelli, Watkins238) selected for contrasting root morphologies. X-ray computed tomography (CT) was applied to examine soil pore networks at cylinder and aggregate scales, while soil hydraulic properties were measured using Wind evaporation and dew point techniques. Results demonstrated significant genotype-driven differences in soil morphology and hydraulic functions. Structural analyses (Minkowski functionals, percolation theory) showed significant variability in bioporosity and pore connectivity among genotypes compared to bare soil. Senatore-Cappelli exhibited notably larger biopores (>1 mm diameter). Hydraulic characterization using a van Genuchten bimodal model revealed statistically significant differences in soil water retention curves and hydraulic conductivity among genotypes. Root traits, including total root length, branching frequency, lateral root length, and root diameter, significantly correlated with soil pore size distribution and hydraulic parameters. This analysis underscores the importance of root architecture in modulating soil structure and water dynamics, highlighting the potential of specific wheat genotypes to affect soil health, water retention, and agricultural sustainability.

papers.title: EFFECTS OF DOLOMITE AMENDMENTS ON PER- AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFAS) LEACHING IN AGRICULTURAL SOILS
papers.summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are often found in agricultural soils due to land application of biosolids, wastewater-derived materials, and atmospheric deposition. However, PFAS transport behavior in variably saturated agricultural soils remains poorly studied. This study evaluates PFAS mobility within unsaturated soil using both intact soil cores (diameter: 3 inches, referred to as large columns (LC)) and packed, homogeneous soil columns (diameter: 1 inch, referred to as small columns (SC)) under the presence and absence of dolomite, which was recently reported to be able to reduce PFAS mobility through adsorption. All columns were amended with a biosolid (Milorganite) and half of the large and small columns received a powdered dolomite amendment at the surface. Columns were subjected to episodic infiltration based on precipitation data from 2019, and the leachate was collected at the base of each column for PFAS analysis. Our results showed that (1) the leaching of PFAS was strongly dependent on the structure and properties of the PFAS, and (2) dolomite amendments could lower the leaching of PFAS. The findings from this research will improve our quantitative understanding of how PFAS move through agricultural soils and the potential risks associated with land application, as well as the design and implementation of science-based management practices and regulation frameworks.

papers.title: Understanding preferential water flow and its contribution to inrush hazard susceptibility in block cave mining : an integrated modelling approach
papers.summary: Water infiltration dynamics in block cave mining are critical to understanding and managing inrush hazards that threaten mine safety and operational continuity. Primary water sources, groundwater aquifers, water-bearing faults, and surface water entering through the subsidence crater interact within the cave muck pile through preferential flow pathways that develop and evolve during mining. How that water then partitions within the broken ore column has received less attention. This research investigates the development and flow behaviour of these pathways using an integrated physical and numerical modelling approach. A conceptual model of a draw column is proposed and tested, characterized by central compressive plug flow zones (PFZ) bounded by finer-grained shear bands (SB1, SB2) that respond differently under unsaturated and saturated conditions. A 76-day quasi-two-dimensional physical experiment, instrumented with seven dielectric moisture sensors and a continuous load-cell mass balance, was complemented by a continuum-flow simulation in MIN3P-HPC, providing an independent benchmark of the within-medium hydraulic behaviour. Grain-size distribution contrasts between the shear bands and plug-flow zones govern infiltration patterns more strongly than geometric position does. The fines-rich shear bands retain three to three-and-a-half times the moisture content of the surrounding plug flow zones across all applied flux conditions. Moisture accumulates by capillary imbibition, drawing water laterally from the PFZ into the fines and holding it against gravity drainage on operationally relevant timescales. Sensor integration and continuum simulation give consistent end-of-experiment within-medium storage of 10.5-11.7 L and 11.75 L, respectively. The simulation also identifies the highest moisture contents along the drawbell walls, flanking the drawpoints, a zone too thin to be resolved by the sensors but implicated as the mechanically weakest plane in the draw column d

papers.title: Study on hydraulic conductivity behaviour with regard to soil characteristics in landfill performance
papers.summary: Municipal solid waste generation continues to increase in Malaysia, placing greater demands on landfill containment systems to effectively prevent leachate migration and protect groundwater resources. The engineering performance of compacted landfill liners depends largely on the hydraulic conductivity achieved after compaction, which is governed by the combined influence of soil physical properties and compaction behaviour. However, the hydraulic performance of landfill-sourced residual soils in Malaysia remains insufficiently understood, particularly regarding the interaction between soil characteristics and hydraulic conductivity under realistic moisture and loading conditions. Therefore, this study investigates the relationship between hydraulic conductivity and residual soil characteristics obtained from the Tanjung Dua Belas (T12) and Air Hitam (AH) landfill sites to evaluate their suitability as compacted landfill liner materials through the development of a preliminary empirical hydraulic conductivity prediction model. Laboratory investigations were conducted in accordance with BS 1377:1990 to determine the physical properties, compaction characteristics and hydraulic conductivity of the investigated soils. Both soils were classified as Silty SAND, with the Tanjung Dua Belas soil exhibiting higher plasticity and moisture sensitivity, whereas the Air Hitam soil exhibited higher particle density. Standard Proctor compaction tests established the Optimum Moisture Content (OMC) and Maximum Dry Density (MDD), followed by specimen preparation at 3% below OMC, OMC and 3% above OMC to simulate field moisture tolerance. Tanjung Dua Belas achieved an MDD of 1.50 g/cm³ at an OMC of 18.56%, while Air Hitam attained an MDD of 1.88 g/cm³ at an OMC of 11.75%. Hydraulic conductivity was evaluated using a modified oedometer under incremental vertical loading from 25 kPa to 200 kPa. At 200 kPa, hydraulic conductivity ranged from 1.241 × 10⁻⁸ cm/s to 3.256 × 10⁻⁸ cm/s across t

papers.title: Integrating ecohydrological, isotopic, and numerical approaches to assess water use by montane Scots pine under varying wetness conditions
papers.source: UPCommons institutional repository (Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya)
papers.summary: (English) Ecohydrology provides a critical framework for understanding interactions between vegetation and the hydrological cycle, particularly in forested ecosystems that strongly regulate water fluxes and ecosystem resilience. In Mediterranean mountain regions, increasing climate variability and recurrent droughts place forests close to their hydraulic limits. Despite these mounting pressures, key uncertainties remain regarding how trees access, store, and utilize water across contrasting wetness conditions, and how these processes can be represented in ecohydrological models. This thesis investigates tree water uptake dynamics and their representation by integrating high temporal- and spatial-resolution field observations, stable water isotopes, and process-based modeling. The study was conducted in the Vallcebre Research Catchments (NE Spain), focusing on Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris L.). Field observations combined meteorological measurements, sap flow and stem diameter variations, soil water content and potential, groundwater levels, and weekly water stable isotopes sampling of precipitation, soil water, groundwater, and xylem water. These data were analyzed using statistical approaches and numerical modeling to examine tree water uptake at the plot scale during contrasting dry and wet periods. Field-based ecohydrological and isotopic analyses revealed that Scots pine water use is strongly constrained by soil water potential during drought, with trees relying on internal stem water storage and showing limited coupling to recent precipitation inputs. Stable isotope evidence demonstrated a dominant contribution of winter-recharged soil water stored in tightly bound soil pores, even following intense summer rainfall events. Only after sustained soil rewetting did trees begin incorporating summer precipitation, ultimately sourcing water from a mixture of winter and summer inputs. papers.title: Combined Rainfall and Snowmelt Effects on Landslide Initiation under a Changing Climate
papers.summary: Klimaendringer forventes å føre til økt nedbørsintensitet, hyppigere ekstremvær og endrede snøsmelteforhold i Norge. Disse endringene kan påvirke poretrykksforholdene i skråninger og dermed øke sannsynligheten for jordskred. Formålet med denne masteroppgaven har vært å undersøke hvordan dagens og fremtidige klimaforhold påvirker skråningsstabiliteten i et studieområde i Trøndelag, med særlig fokus på samspillet mellom nedbør og snøsmelting. Oppgaven bygger på teori om umettet jordmekanikk, infiltrasjonsprosesser og utløsning av jordskred. For å analysere skråningsstabilitet under ulike klimascenarioer ble den fysisk baserte skråningsstabilitetsmodellen PyTRI benyttet. Modellen simulerer transient infiltrasjon, poretrykkutvikling og sikkerhetsfaktor i skråninger som utsettes for varierende vanntilførsel. Historiske data for nedbør og snøsmelting fra Varsom Senorge ble brukt til å etablere kombinerte intensitet-varighet-frekvens (IVF) kurver for dagens klima. Disse representerer den samlede hydrologiske effekten fra nedbør og snøsmelting. Deretter ble klimaprognoser benyttet til å utvikle tilsvarende kurver for fremtidige nedbørs- og snøsmelteforhold, som ble analysert for å vurdere hvordan disse kan påvirke skråningsstabiliteten i et fremtidig klima. Resultatene viser at økt nedbør generelt fører til større ustabile områder og flere celler med sikkerhetsfaktor lavere enn en. Kombinerte hendelser med både nedbør og snøsmelting ga de største ustabile områdene, noe som indikerer at snøsmelting kan være en viktig utløsende faktor i tillegg til intens nedbør. Sensitivitetsanalysene viste videre at endringer i snøsmelteforhold kan ha betydelig innvirkning på skråningsstabiliteten, særlig ved økte smeltemengder. Funnene tyder på at klimaendringer kan bidra til økt skredfare i Trøndelag gjennom endringer i både nedbørs- og snøsmelteforhold, noe som kan føre til økt vanninnhold i jorda og høyere poretrykk i skråninger. Resultatene er imidlertid forbundet med usikkerhet knytte

papers.title: Time-Lapse 3D Electrical Resistivity Tomography to Resolve Preferential Flow Paths in a Forestry Hillslope supported by a Brilliant Blue Tracer
papers.summary: Understanding subsurface water movement, particularly preferential water flow, is critical for water resource management and predicting contaminant transport. However, traditional invasive methods like dye staining experiments are destructive and only provide static information. Consequently, this thesis investigates the effectiveness of 3D time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) for monitoring infiltration dynamics on a forested hillslope in Lower Austria. A Brilliant Blue saline tracer was applied to a 0.8 × 0.8 m plot during a two-hour irrigation event. ERT measurements were collected at 7-minute intervals and processed using various inversion strategies to resolve resistivity changes over time. The resistivity data were then used to delineate preferential flow paths and estimate pore water velocities.The ERT monitoring successfully captured the decrease in resistivity, directly corresponding to the infiltration of the tracer.The wetting front migrated rapidly to a depth of 0.25 m within the first 45 minutes before slowing to a maximum of 0.28 m at the end of the irrigation. Pore water velocities, derived from resistivity breakthrough curves, varied from 0.0002 cm/min in the soil matrix to up to 6 cm/min in localized preferential flow paths. Comparison of the ERT inversion results with the post-excavation Brilliant Blue staining patterns confirmed that the centers of conductive anomalies align with the staining patterns, although discrete macropores and root channels could not beresolved due to the limited resolution of the method.These results demonstrate that 3D time-lapse ERT is a robust, non-invasive tool for quantifying the spatio-temporal dynamics of preferential flow, though its resolution remains constrained by the electrode array geometry and the inherent smoothing of the inversion process.

Study of methodological approaches for biodiversity monitoring in Nature-based Solutions (NBS) interventions, using Soil and Water Bioengineering (SWBE) techniques in the Mediterranean region.
papers.summary: In the context of the current climate crisis, the intensification of extreme meteoro-logical events necessitates a shift in hydrogeological risk-mitigation strategies, promoting a transition toward Nature-Based Solutions (NBS). Among these, Soil and Water Bioengineer-ing (SWBE) represent a bioinspired solution for slope stabilisation, as it combines geotech-nical safety with the restoration of ecological functionality. However, the scientific valida-tion of such techniques is often caught up in disciplinary fragmentation and by the lack of long-term monitoring protocols capable of assessing both the evolution of slope stability and the success of environmental recovery. This study aims to address this gap through the development and application of an integrated, multidisciplinary monitoring approach. The research focuses on shallow landslides in the Northwest Tuscany (Pomezzana case study, 1996 flood events), comparing sites restored using SWBE techniques and naturally evolved landslides. Subsequently, the core of the research focused on a dual-phase long-term monitoring campaign, focusing on both slope stability and ecological recovery. The first phase involved a comparative stability analysis between a landslide restored with SWBE techniques and an adjacent landslide left to natural evolution. Data acquired from the multi-approach protocol were incorporated into slope-stability modelling to quantify the temporal evolution of the Factor of Safety. The results demonstrate that, in the SWBE restored site, the physiological degradation of wooden structural elements is effectively compensated by the progressive in-crease in soil-root reinforcement. This dynamic equilibrium ensures that the Factor of Safe-ty remains stable over time, contrasting with the fluctuations observed in the natural evolu-tion scenario. Assessing metal mobility of industrially sourced NI and CU in Sudbury, Ontario, Canada peatlands
papers.summary: Peatlands are essential ecosystems globally, acting as important areas of carbon storage. However, as industrial pollution has increased in the last two centuries peatlands are now acting as landscape stores of potentially toxic metals (PTMs). The subsequent storage of these PTMs has degraded ecosystem services in many peatlands, altering plant composition, changing the hydro physical structure of the peat, and eliminating many keystone peatland species such as Sphagnum moss. Most importantly, these large stores of PTMs pose a potential risk to hydrologically connected ecosystems if they are remobilized. With an increased focus on restoring these contaminated peatlands through Sphagnum moss reintroduction, itis uncertain how PTMs may be remobilized as the geochemical conditions and hydrological properties of these sites are changed. Therefore, it is critical that the hydro physical and geochemical processes and properties influencing PTM mobility are better understood in these contaminated peatlands. To improve our understanding of PTM mobility and transport in contaminated peatlands, three peatlands with varying levels of contamination and recovery were identified in Sudbury, Ontario, Canada. The identified contamination gradient was used with the objective of assessing how the reintroduction of Sphagnum moss would influence PTM transport. Over three field seasons (May-October; 2023-2025)biweekly grab samples (dissolved organic matter; DOM), trace metals, and major anions) and hydrological measurements (saturated hydraulic conductivity, weekly water table position) were gathered from preinstalled wells and piezometers at all three sites. Field results show that nickel (Ni) and copper (Cu)relative transport was determined by a combination of varying biogeochemical and hydrological conditions, with relative Ni and Cu transport lowest at Low-PTM likely due to the burial and consolidation of the contaminated layer. papers.title: Soil characteristics of flood control dikes along the Morava-Thaya River in eastern Austria : effects of environmental factors and dike management
papers.source: Epsilon Archive for Student Projects (Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences)
papers.summary: This study investigates the interactions between soil physical, chemical and biological parameters as well as the influence of climatic, environmental and spatial components on them in the context of dike stability along the Morava-Thaya river system in Central Europe. Climatic variability with more frequent droughts and extreme precipitation events in the future, induced through climate change, might affect flood protection systems through changes in soil structure, hydrology and biogeochemical processes. This study aims to identify dominant environmental gradients, site-specific variability and assess the potential implications for dike stability in the mentioned region. In total, 20 dike sites, including 4 measurement points on the landside and waterside were taken into consideration together with management practices, exposition, distance to agriculture and to forest as well as location along the dam. Soil texture, bulk density, aggregate stability, organic matter fractions, nutrient availability, microbial biomass, enzyme activities, soil moisture, and temperature were analyzed together with climatic variables. The results revealed a pronounced spatial heterogeneity along the dam. Coarse-textured sandy sites with lower moisture, reduced microbial biomass, weaker macroaggregate stability and lower organic carbon content could favor piping, seepage and internal erosion. On the other hand, finer-textured sites exhibited stronger aggregation, greater nutrient availability and increased microbial biomass. There, an increase in water retention capacities could occur, but also an increase in vulnerability to shrink-swell dynamics, desiccation cracking and preferential flow formation during drought periods. Organic carbon, microbial biomass, nutrient availability and macroaggregate stability are indicators of biologically mediated aggregation processes, which can contribute to structural cohesion of dike soils. papers.title: Säätösalaojitus ja ilmastonmuutos suomalaisessa maataloudessa
papers.summary: Agricultural water management plays a key role in sustainable crop production. Controlled drainage has been proposed as a method for mitigating the environmental impacts of drained agricultural lands and adapting to meteorological variability and climate change. However, there remains a lack of quantitative understanding of how controlled drainage influences field-scale hydrology across different soil types and climatic conditions. A process-based hydrological model was used to simulate the field-scale hydrological effects of controlled drainage in comparison to conventional free drainage in Finland. The main objective was to quantify the effects on groundwater table depths and field water balance and analyze how the effects change during the 21st century due to climate change. The simulations applied both mineral soil and peatland parameterizations. Furthermore, the dissertation addressed the following objectives: 1) to analyze the hydrology and performance of controlled drainage on a peatland field with a strong groundwater connection to an upslope forest area, 2) to couple hydrological simulations with peat subsidence under controlled drainage, and 3) to simulate the combination of controlled drainage and open ditch damming and assess the spatial distribution of the effects on groundwater table depths. The simulation results showed controlled drainage to be a viable method to reduce groundwater table depth, with even growing season groundwater table depths being reduced by 0.06–0.26 m. Especially when storing water in the field during earlier months, controlled drainage has potential to reduce growing season drought risk and the environmental impacts of deep groundwater levels. Drain discharge was reduced by 7–23%. This was reflected in increased lateral groundwater outflow, which may be beneficial in reducing substance load, but the peatland simulations showed also a strong increase in surface layer runoff. papers.title: Corn yield, water productivity, and soil hydraulics under deficit irrigation with biochar and APSA-80 in Southwest Kansas
papers.summary: The increasing rate of groundwater extraction from the Ogallala Aquifer, combined with lithologic and statutory limitations, imposes a possible reduction of water use by corn producers irrigating in southwest Kansas. During the cropping season of 2025, this field study analyzed the effects of deficit irrigation (W100 (203.2 mm) and W50 (101.6 mm)) as well as IBI-certified granular softwood biochar (0, 1, and 3.5 t ha⁻¹) and APSA-80 non-ionic soil surfactant (presence/absence) on corn grain yield, irrigation water productivity (IWP), and soil hydraulic parameters in a research experiment on the soils of Southwest Research-Extension Center (SWREC), Garden City, Finney County, Kansas. The design of the experiment involved a balanced split-plot RCBD design with three replications (n=36 subplots) of Ulysses silt loam soil in a no-till system. Irrigation was the whole-plot variable, and biochar and APSA-80 were subplot variables. Pre- and post-treatment field-saturated hydraulic conductivity (Kfs) was measured using a SATURO dual-head infiltrometer, and volumetric water content (VWC) at 10 cm depth was measured at four growth stages using Acclima TDR probes. The total seasonal precipitation was 284.2 mm, 115.1 mm of which fell after September. W50 irrigation produced a yield loss of only 7.1% (12,011.67 kg ha-1 vs. 12,925.60 kg ha-1; F1,2 = 8.904, p = 0.0964, †). On the other hand, IWP increased by 85.9% (118.22 vs. 63.61 kg ha⁻¹ mm⁻¹; F1,2 = 606.31, p = 0.0016, **). This demonstrates the economic and agronomic advantages of deficit irrigation under the constraint of Ogallala allocation. The yield loss was shown to have the same trend in all three blocks, but because of the conservative character of the test with df = 2, significance was not achieved at α = 0.05.
